התקווה. סיפורה של שכונה: Hatikva. The Story of a Neighborhood
From its founding, the Hatikva neighborhood was a trailblazer. Its residents, an ingathering of cultures and communities, created an independent, pioneering community built on mutual responsibility, giving, creativity and determination, values that helped it face a long series of great challenges over the years. This heritage is an inseparable part of the story of Hatikva and will accompany the neighborhood into the future.

אמיר חודורוב (1957) הוא צלם ואמן חזותי,: Amir Chodorov (b. 1957) is a photographer and visual artist, creator and developer of the "Wholeness Photography" method. Chodorov, a former fighter pilot in the Israeli Air Force, lives and works in Tel Aviv and has been active in photography and art for more than four decades.
לאורך השנים פיתח שפה אמנותית ייחודית המח: Over the years he has developed a unique artistic language that combines photography, planning and composition, and he holds the registered trademark ®AC Amir Chodorov Wholeness Photography (trademark no. 345459, valid until 11.11.2031). His works have been shown in galleries, museums and private and public collections in Israel and around the world.
שורשיה של תפיסתו האמנותית של חודורוב נטו: The roots of Chodorov's artistic outlook were planted many years earlier. At the age of 17 he visited the Sistine Chapel in Rome for the first time.
מול התקרה רחבת־הממדים של מיכלאנג׳לו התגב: Facing Michelangelo's vast ceiling, a thought took shape in him that would stay with him through the years: this is how narratives should be told – on a grand scale, totally, in a way that invites the eye to wander among the parts of the work rather than fix on a single point. That encounter later became one of the sources that shaped his artistic outlook.
בהמשך שירת חודורוב במשך 25 שנים בחיל האו: Chodorov went on to serve 25 years in the Israeli Air Force, years in which he grew used to looking at the world from above as well. Alongside his service he kept photographing constantly, out of love for photography, while the encounter with the Renaissance works and the ideas they had awakened in him in Rome continued to accompany him.
כ־15 שנים לאחר שחרורו מצה״ל שב חודורוב ל: Some 15 years after his discharge from the IDF, Chodorov returned to Rome and Florence, this time wishing to delve into the Renaissance works and the way they were made. There he discovered what he saw as the secret of the Renaissance masters: preparation. He learned that each work was preceded by an orderly, in-depth process – research into the figures and the story, precise planning of composition and perspective based on mathematics first written by Plato and Euclid, and the gradual construction of a large work out of many parts.
מתוך העקרונות האלה פיתח חודורוב את שיטת: From these principles Chodorov developed the "Wholeness Photography" method. Instead of settling for a single frame, he shoots hundreds and sometimes thousands of photographs from different angles and joins them into one large-scale work. Every detail stands on its own, yet takes on its full meaning as part of the whole.
כשהחל חודורוב לתכנן את אתר ההנצחה בחניון: When Chodorov began planning the memorial site at the Re'im parking lot, he returned to the Renaissance masters' idea of preparation. He studied in depth the stories behind the names – the people, their lives, their loves and their dreams – and from them began to shape the space he saw in his mind's eye.
לאורך התהליך ליוותה אותו תפיסתו של מיכלא: Throughout the process he was guided by Michelangelo's view that a work is born first in thought, while its realization in matter is the way to give it expression. This is how Chodorov saw the Re'im parking lot too – as a large-scale work on the soil of the Negev, where beauty and sorrow exist side by side. An attempt to create wholeness in a place where the heart was shattered to pieces.
לאורך השנים זכה חודורוב להכרה בינלאומית,: Over the years Chodorov has won international recognition, and his works have been shown in museums, galleries and private and corporate collections in Israel and around the world.
בין ההכרות והפרסים שקיבל: הפרס הראשון בב: Among the honors and awards he has received: first prize at the London Art Biennale 2019, inclusion in the Top 60 Masters list in New York (2022), and recognition as a Maestro by Art Academy Italy. His works have been shown at, among others, the Vatican Museum, the Leonardo da Vinci Museum in Milan and the Holon Museum.
בין הפרויקטים רחבי ההיקף שיצר נמנים: ״קי: His large-scale projects include: the "Heritage Walls" in Tel Aviv's Hatikva neighborhood, covering some 1,200 m²; a work depicting the Old City of Jerusalem at Binyanei HaUma in Jerusalem; and a permanent 6.5-meter installation at the IDF General Staff headquarters in the Kirya, Tel Aviv.

בדצמבר 2022 הזמין אותי גיא זוזות, מנהל ב: In December 2022, Guy Zuzut, director of Beit Dani, invited me to join him as an artist and tell the story of the Hatikva neighborhood since its founding in 1935. In the four years since, I have read some 5,000 documents from the British Mandate period and the State Archives, and 1,200 m² of heritage walls and artworks have been created at Beit Dani, the Bnei Yehuda club, Dohal Hall, the Yoram Levinstein theater and throughout the neighborhood – and the project is not finished yet.

כאמן יוצר, שעיצב והקים פרויקטים גדולים כ: As an artist who has designed and built large projects such as "The Re'im Parking Lot – Memorial Site", the heritage story of the Borochov neighborhood in Givatayim and many other projects in Israel and abroad, I have learned that every place tells a story. But the Hatikva neighborhood was different: even the Re'im parking lot project began right here, in a meeting at Beit Dani with the mother of the late Ilan Moshe Yaakov, who was murdered at the Nova festival, and in the decision to create the collage of the murdered. From the moment I was exposed to the wealth of material, the neighborhood was seared into my heart with a love that is hard to explain: a love for the beauty and creativity of its residents over 90 years, who, despite the many hardships, knew how to join hands and create this wonderful pearl.
חשבתי לעצמי תוך כדי העבודה על סיפור המור: While working on the heritage story I thought to myself that this small neighborhood, which stretches over only some 77 streets and takes about 20 minutes to cross, could serve as a true social model for the State of Israel in these days – a model that knew how to unite the disconnected throughout its existence, that knew how to quarrel, love, produce and advance, all while leaning on three guiding, uniting values that worked within it like an engine of infinite power: accepting the other, determination and action, and giving for the sake of giving.
Thank you for the privilege of being a partner in its story.
מן העיתונות: ידיעות תל אביב על הפרויקט: From the press: Yedioth Tel Aviv on the project
קשה עוד יותר שלא להתאהב בתושבי השכונה, ב: It is even harder not to fall in love with the neighborhood's residents, with the spirit that beats in it, its glorious history, the community synagogues, the colorful market, the local art, the miracle called Beit Dani, the magic of Gan HaTikva and even its special architecture.
למרבה הצער, בימים אלו מתמודדת השכונה עם: Sadly, the neighborhood is now facing a process of communal and cultural disintegration, added to a negative stigma that has followed it for many years. The worrying present is damaging the consciousness of its residents, at least some of whom are losing faith in its future.
חוברת זו היא חלק מניסיון חשוב לבלום את ה: This booklet is part of an important attempt to halt this process. It embodies the effort to celebrate the story of the Hatikva neighborhood, which is not told enough and not known as it deserves to be, not even by its own residents. It seeks to present Hatikva as a place of spiritual, human and cultural richness.
הניסיון האמור לא נועד רק עבור השכונה עצמ: This attempt is not meant for the neighborhood alone. In a time of worsening social polarization, "the wisdom of Hatikva" is a message and an inspiration for all of Israeli society. It is the wisdom of living together, of mutual responsibility and accepting the other, of creating a heterogeneous whole greater than the sum of its parts, of the dialogue of the street as an alternative to screens of objectification and division. It is also the wisdom of coping with social crises, the determination to break new ground, and the ability to channel hardship into a life of community and creation.
יש תקווה בשכונת התקווה, אבל זה לא אומר ש: There is hope in Hatikva, but that does not mean it is perfect. Its beauty is not the fashion-magazine kind, and its values were not invented by marketing and advertising agencies. There are also those who, in order to hear the sounds of its message, must first clear away the background noise of false images and prejudice. This booklet is meant for them too.
בנסיבות בהן צמחה, שכונת התקווה היא פלא י: Given the circumstances in which it grew, the Hatikva neighborhood is an Israeli wonder that we ought to learn about and understand, so that we may love it and protect it together and it will not be lost. As the environmentalist Baba Dioum said: "In the end we will conserve only what we love, we will love only what we understand, and we will understand only what we are taught."
תבוא הברכה, האהבה והתקווה לכל מי שסייע,: May blessing, love and hope come to all who have helped, are helping and will help to protect Hatikva and its values.

השלם הגדול של אמיר חודורוב: The Great Whole of Amir Chodorov
מבוא: פילוסופיה של שלמות ואיזון: Introduction: A Philosophy of Wholeness and Balance
בעולם העכשווי המאופיין בפרגמנטציה דורסני: In today's world, marked by relentless fragmentation, visual noise and an unceasing flood of broken shards of images, the striving for harmony is not merely an aesthetic choice but an existential human need for "repair" (tikkun). Indeed, at the center of Amir Chodorov's work stands the philosophy of "wholeness" – a philosophy meant not only to answer the human need to bridge the gap between the individual and the collective, but, more importantly, to fill the spaces between the fragments of images and scraps of information that flood our world. To this end Chodorov developed the idea of "Wholeness Photography", which is not merely an artistic practice that builds one picture out of thousands of photographs taken from a wealth of angles, but an artistic doctrine that seeks to turn the "incomprehensible" and the "unknown" into the familiar and the known. For the viewer, who has grown used to consuming reality through snippets of information – visual, verbal and aural – scattered across social networks as shards of images, the idea of Wholeness Photography offers a cognitive and emotional anchor. For this is not just an artistic technique but a striving for visual wholeness, for creating a kind of "safe space" of order within chaos. This connection between inner vision and outer reality is realized through a masterful craft of taking apart and reassembling, which converts the scattered digital image into a continuum of wholeness by way of Sisyphean, spiritual handiwork.
מלאכת הפסיפס המודרנית: מן הרנסנס ועד העד: The Modern Craft of Mosaic: From the Renaissance to the Lens
חודורוב אינו \"לוכד\" רגעים הוא בונה אות: Chodorov does not "capture" moments; he builds them into a continuum of time and place. In his view, photography is a strategic act of architectural construction, in which each work is composed of hundreds and sometimes thousands of separate photographs, just as contemporary reality itself is made. Each single photograph is a kind of "pixel" that becomes a philosophical atom in a larger structure, much like the historical craft of mosaic, which gives the whole a power greater than the sum of its parts. Nor is the link to the Renaissance in Chodorov's work a coincidence. In 1553 Ascanio Condivi published an official, authorized biography of Michelangelo, written under the full supervision of the master himself and largely based on his own words. In it Condivi claimed that the great artist grew up in a house of stonecutters (scarpellini) and thus drank in his love of the chisel with his wet-nurse's milk. As a sculptor-painter, Michelangelo joined separate narratives in the Sistine Chapel – from the Creation of the world to the Flood – into a balanced spiritual experience of space and spirit. A special example is the figure of the prophet Jonah: Michelangelo used sharp perspective to "break" the physical limitation of the curved ceiling, to burst the bounds of the standard two-dimensional frame and create a space in which the multitude of details no longer confuses perception but instead heightens the viewer's sense of standing before the truth.
בהשאלה, ניתן לומר כי חודורוב, כ\"סתת דיג: By analogy, one may say that Chodorov, as a "digital stonecutter", extracts the image from mountains of visual information with surgical precision; he uses Wholeness as one who "tiles" reality with mosaic stones. The idea of mosaic – assembling a whole rich in meaning from single, separate pieces – became in Western thought, and sometimes already in antiquity itself, a powerful philosophical metaphor. There is something paradoxical about mosaic: the artist is seemingly limited to a finite number of pieces that might constrain him, and yet he produces an unexpected wealth of hues, movement and illusion of depth. It is precisely the restriction to a finite number of "building blocks" that gives mosaic its flexibility: the ability to "move a single stone" and give it new meaning within the whole makes the medium surprisingly flexible and versatile. It is no accident, then, that thinkers of every generation, and above all in the ancient world, saw the world itself as a kind of mosaic-cosmos: a fabric of seemingly separate parts – events, people, fates – that ultimately compose a harmonious, purposeful cosmic pattern (logos), even if from the individual point of view the overall pattern cannot be seen at all. Likewise, memory and history themselves can be understood as a mosaic: just as a physical mosaic usually survives only in partial fragments and still gives us a true picture, so our knowledge of the world is a "mosaic" of its own – fragments of testimony, partial texts, from which we try, carefully and meticulously, to reconstruct a whole picture.
המדיום הוא המסר: המצלמה כשלוחה של המוח: The Medium Is the Message: The Camera as an Extension of the Mind
על פי משנתו של מרשל מקלוהן: \"המדיום הוא: According to Marshall McLuhan's teaching that "the medium is the message", in Chodorov's work too technology is not merely a technical tool but an extension of the mind and of perception – a perception that makes it possible to translate inner spatial vision into tangible reality. In a world of "noise media", the very method of work – the Sisyphean gathering of a thousand fragments and their organization into a single unit – is a message of unity and synthesis. Chodorov acts as "an artist who dictates reality" rather than one who merely reflects it. He removes the optical distortions and failings of ordinary lenses to create a "corrected reality". Here lies the link to the Renaissance concept of Ideal Beauty: the artist does not copy nature as it is, but "perfects" it to reveal the higher, ordered truth hidden within it.
המעבר מצלם מתעד למעצב תפיסה מאפשר לצופה: The shift from documenting photographer to shaper of perception allows the viewer to experience a space in which the eye and the mind wander undisturbed, within a reality that is at once familiar and yet perfect in a way that ordinary human sight cannot achieve.
הגיאומטריה של הרוח: הרמוניה אלוהית וסדר: The Geometry of the Spirit: Divine Harmony and Cosmic Order
מכאן, לא מפתיע שהיופי בעבודותיו של חודור: Hence it is not surprising that the beauty of Chodorov's works is anchored in the mathematics of the universe. As Pythagoras, Euclid, Plato and Kepler taught us, geometry and mathematics are the languages in which the book of nature is written. Chodorov's wholeness rests on "the signature of cosmic harmony", namely the golden rules: the use of the golden ratio (Phi – 1.618), the Fibonacci sequence and the golden angle (137.5°). These patterns, which appear in nature – in pine cones and sunflowers, for example – ensure infinite division without overlaps or "holes", and explain why the work feels "right" and calming to the viewer in a biological, instinctive way. In this spirit, Chodorov's work echoes "the theory of the three spheres" and the wisdom of the Platonic Solids – the five perfect geometric bodies (tetrahedron, cube, octahedron and so on) that Plato linked to the elements of the universe in the "Timaeus". An especially profound insight is the discovery that the ratio between the outer (circumscribed) sphere and the inner (inscribed) sphere is exactly the same for all the Platonic solids. This is the mathematical code of absolute balance. Space, for instance, is hyperbolic – that is, nature does not build straight, linear grids but hyperbolic space. And so Chodorov, in his mastery of lens distortion, in fact returns photography to the organic, non-linear truth of nature. The use of these laws makes photography a work that does not merely represent aesthetics but reflects the divine order hidden beneath the surface of matter.
סיכום: הזמנה למדיטציה חזותית: Conclusion: An Invitation to Visual Meditation
המפגש עם \"Wholeness Photography\" הוא ה: The encounter with "Wholeness Photography" is an invitation to what is now called "slow looking" or "sustained looking", in a reality that sanctifies the fast and the superficial; Amir Chodorov's works thus offer a space of visual meditation. They invite the visitor to stop, to breathe and to carry out an "inner repair" through contemplation. The viewer is invited to get seemingly lost among the thousands of small details – the pixels that are the building blocks of the modern mosaic – in order ultimately to find "the great whole". It is a moment of renewed connection with the great harmony of the world, in which mathematics becomes spirit and photography becomes a prayer of order and beauty. Nature works as a great mathematician – and art is the reflection of that perfection.

He was murdered at the Nova festival on 7.10.23, at only 29. Ilan was a friend, a leader and an educator; modest and admired, determined and devoted; a connector and a helper, a believer and a lover – with a heart as big as the world for every person.

As a child and a teenager he was active at the "Beit Dani" community center, which became his second home. עם שחרורו שב לבית דני, מתוך תחושת שליחות: On his discharge he returned to Beit Dani out of a deep sense of mission and devoted his life to education and leadership. He soon stood out for his abilities and values, advanced from youth counselor to coordinator, and finally served as director of the youth center and of the "Yesh Matzav LeManash" program. In all his roles he excelled and was a true inspiration.
אחת מחניכותיו ספדה לו במילים מרגשות: \"א: One of his youth group members eulogized him in moving words: "Ilan is a name from the plant world describing an impressive, amazing tree, and you were exactly that! A tree full of strength, beauty and roots. Amazing in beauty and character, and from you grew many branches – children and people who took from you all the good you gave the world."
גם ברגעיו האחרונים לא חשב אילן על עצמו א: Even in his last moments Ilan thought not of himself but of his community and his country. In a phone call from the festival, minutes before he was murdered, he asked that the shelter at Beit Dani be opened for the residents of the neighborhood he loved so much. When the sirens sounded he posted an unforgettable video on social media that became a testament of leadership and faith.
אילן אהב את החיים וחי כל רגע באלף צבעים:: Ilan loved life and lived every moment in a thousand colors: he prayed and made up the minyan at the Bukharan synagogue, surfed and danced, studied at the University of Haifa, was the glue of his family and filled everyone around him with endless joy. He traveled to more than 40 countries, but always came back and stressed: Beit Dani and the Hatikva neighborhood – this is home. Here he educated his youth groups, and here he dreamed of raising his children.
ואנו נמשיך בדרכו, באורו וברוחו. ניטע עוד: And we will continue in his path, in his light and in his spirit. We will plant more and more roots – tree after tree of unconditional love and good deeds.
יהי זכרו ברוך: May his memory be a blessing
בשנת 1935, תחת שלטון המנדט הבריטי, חצה א: In 1935, under the British Mandate, a unique group of Sephardi, Yemenite and Ashkenazi settlers crossed Wadi Musrara – today the Ayalon stream – and together founded an independent, pioneering settlement. Only in 1948, when it was already a vibrant neighborhood of 18,000 residents, was "Hatikva" annexed to the city of Tel Aviv. From its founding, the neighborhood broke new ground in education, culture, music, cuisine, leadership and community.
סיפור הקמתה של השכונה הוא בבחינת ניצחון: The story of the neighborhood's founding is a heroic victory over harsh and complex starting conditions, together with an ingathering of different people from different lands of origin who, despite their differences, labored together to build a shared home against all odds. It is a story of the heroism of a community that became independent and close-knit, and created a rich, thriving culture built on deep tradition alongside openness to modernity.

ההיסטוריה של שכונת התקווה שזורה בתולדות: The history of the Hatikva neighborhood is interwoven with the history of the founding of the State of Israel. On 8 December 1947 the neighborhood saw the first major military clash of the War of Independence, which opened with an Arab attack and ended in a heroic victory for the neighborhood's defenders.
חסן סַלמֶה, מפקד הכוח הערבי באזור, הוביל: Hassan Salameh, commander of the Arab force in the area, led hundreds of fighters who sought to surprise the "Haganah" forces in Hatikva and the neighboring Ezra and Beit Yaakov neighborhoods. The attackers began seizing houses and setting them on fire, driving hundreds of residents northward.
כוח תגבור מיוחד הגיע לעזרת השכונה עם נשק: A special reinforcement force came to the neighborhood's aid with weapons and ammunition, and the fighting ended with a call for a ceasefire by the British Mandate authorities. The outcome of the battle for Hatikva placed it in the pantheon of Israeli heroism: despite being outnumbered in fighters and ammunition, the neighborhood's defenders thwarted the Arab plan without loss of life.
גיבור הקרב היה עזרא צפדיה, יליד לבנון, ש: The hero of the battle was Ezra Tzafadia, born in Lebanon, who thanks to his command of Arabic managed to mislead the attackers and draw them into an ambush in a narrow alley. Tzafadia, only 16 at the time of the battle, lost an eye in the fighting and received a commendation for his bravery. He later turned to social activism and founded children's choirs at the "Tiferet Israel" and "Magen David" synagogues.
השטח שבו התחולל הקרב הפך כעבור שנים אחדו: A few years later the ground where the battle took place became a public park, created on the initiative of the Tel Aviv municipality for the benefit of the neighborhood's residents. Gan HaTikva was inaugurated on 21 July 1954, the 50th Hebrew anniversary of the death of the visionary of the state, Theodor (Binyamin Ze'ev) Herzl.
כבר מראשיתו שימש גן התקווה מרחב של פנאי: From the start Gan HaTikva served as a space for leisure and meeting for the residents. Today it houses a small community center that began as a branch of Beit Dani, and it is a focus for celebrations and community events: the traditional Hanukkah torch parade, Adloyada processions on Purim, tree planting on Tu BiShvat and national celebrations on Independence Day.
התקווה - עוד לא אבדה!: Hatikva – Our Hope Is Not Yet Lost!
הרבה מסתורין אפף את שכונת התקווה בראשית: Much mystery surrounded the Hatikva neighborhood in its early days. One striking example is the ambiguity about the origin of its name. According to one version, the name commemorates a farm called "Mount Hope" (Har HaTikva), founded nearby by Christian settlers from the USA and Germany in the 19th century.
הסבר אחר תולה את הבחירה בשם ביהושע ליכטר: Another explanation attributes the choice of name to Yehoshua Lichter, one of the neighborhood's founders, who linked its founding to the realization of the Zionist dream. There is also the view that the "hope" in the name is the first residents' hope for a better future.
אומרים ששם הוא ראי לנשמה, ואם כך הדבר לא: They say a name is a mirror of the soul, and if so it is no surprise that the story of Hatikva is a story of optimism and faith. The neighborhood's name embodies its essence and seems to have foreseen its fate, its future and its destiny.
השכונה היא גם קפסולה מזוקקת שאוצרת בתוכה: The neighborhood is also a distilled capsule holding the essence of Judaism and Israeliness in one word – hope (tikva). A central element of Judaism is the expectation of a better future and the work toward realizing it. It is an element that nourishes Israeliness too, and it is no accident that the national anthem is called "HaTikva" – "The Hope".
התקווה והאמונה כרוכות זו בזו, כיוון שהתק: Hope and faith are bound up with one another, because hope is present wherever a person believes in their ability to rise beyond themselves. The Hatikva neighborhood is the dwelling-place of hope: the place where hope is present like the Divine Presence, giving life to a person even in their hardest moments.
מקור השם: מה אומרים המסמכים: The Origin of the Name: What the Documents Say
בחוברת מוצגות שלוש גרסאות לשם השכונה: הח: The booklet presents three versions of the neighborhood's name: the "Mount Hope" farm, Yehoshua Lichter and the Zionist dream, and the residents' hope. Here we checked the first two against sources from the same period. The result is fairly clear: the Lichter version has a chain of documents behind it, and the "Mount Hope" version has none.
הקשר החזק: הדרך של ליכטר אל \"התקווה\": The Strong Link: Lichter's Road to "Hatikva"
ליכטר מייסד את השבועון הרוויזיוניסטי \"ח: Lichter founds the Revisionist weekly "Hazit HaAm". The editor-in-chief is Dr. Yehoshua Yeivin, and Abba Achimeir writes for it.
בחקירת רצח ארלוזורוב ליכטר עומד במסדר זי: In the investigation of the Arlosoroff murder, Lichter stands in a police line-up. Mrs. Arlosoroff says he "resembles the shooter in type, but he is not the man".
בגיליון המאה של \"חזית העם\" מתפרסם המאמ: The hundredth issue of "Hazit HaAm" publishes the article "HaTikva" (The Hope). It declares that hope is not passive longing but "the Zionist program", "our ideal" and "our means of war". In the same issue Achimeir and Yeivin bless Lichter "to work, to suffering and to hope".
ליכטר, אחימאיר, ייבין ואחרים מורשעים במש: Lichter, Achimeir, Yeivin and others are convicted in the "Brit HaBiryonim" trial and imprisoned in Jaffa prison. According to "Herut" (1948), Abu Hadra sat with them in cell 6, and Lichter came out of there with a lease on his orange groves.
ליכטר נכנס לשותפות עם סטנדרד בנק וחברת \: Lichter goes into partnership with Standard Bank and the "HaMeyashev" company. In August the first advertisements for "the Hatikva neighborhood" appear in "HaYarden", the paper that replaced "Hazit HaAm". In the 1935 advertisements the name appears for the first time; before that it does not appear in the press at all.
ליכטר מקבל את רישיון הנשק הראשון בשכונה,: Lichter receives the neighborhood's first firearms license, to guard the land he had founded.
השרשרת הזאת מראה איך המילה עברה אצל ליכט: This chain shows how, for Lichter, the word moved from slogan to program, and from program to place. His newspaper turned "HaTikva" from an anthem of longing into a call to action. He received a blessing signed "and to hope" from his comrades, sat in prison with them, came out with the land, and a year later his neighborhood was called "Hatikva" in the newspaper of the same movement.
\"הר התקווה\" (Mount Hope) הייתה חווה חק: "Mount Hope" (Har HaTikva) was an agricultural farm founded in 1853 by millenarian Christians from the United States and Prussia, among them Clorinda Minor and the Grosssteinbeck family, northeast of Jaffa. The farm was abandoned as early as 1858.
אין לקשר הזה שום עוגן מתקופת ההקמה. בעית: This link has no anchor at all in the founding period. In the Hebrew press between 1925 and 1948 there is not a single mention of "Har HaTikva". The sources describing the farm also place it in the area of today's Montefiore neighborhood, several kilometers from Abu Hadra's orange grove. The link appears only in later writing, probably as a connection between two places that happen to bear a similar name.
אין בידינו משפט מפורש מ־1935 שאומר \"קרא: We do not have an explicit sentence from 1935 saying "we named the neighborhood this because…". Nor is the article "HaTikva" signed. So the explanation is a conclusion strongly supported by the documents, not direct testimony.
הגרסה השלישית, תקוותם של התושבים לעתיד ט: The third version, the residents' hope for a better future, does not contradict Lichter. The name was given from above, out of ideology, and the residents, mostly Mizrahi and Yemenite families, gave it their own meaning over the years.

This model, which grew in the neighborhood together with the Neighborhood Renewal Project, became the basis for local neighborhood leadership that was replicated elsewhere in the country.

Above them all stands out the 1979 visit of President Yitzhak Navon: in March of that year President Navon stayed in the neighborhood for three full days, to get to know it closely and to raise its standing in the eyes of its residents and of the whole country.
במהלך הביקור הסתובב הנשיא ברחבי השכונה,: During the visit the President walked around the neighborhood, met residents at random and held in-depth conversations with them, met public figures, community leaders and Bnei Yehuda players, visited educational and cultural institutions and the health clinic, went on tours and learning sessions, visited the market and the youth and senior clubs, was hosted by the neighborhood's founders and rabbis and slept in residents' homes. The President placed special emphasis on meeting children and teenagers, whom he encouraged to dream big and aim as high as they possibly could.
הוא שמע מהתושבים ומהצוותים החינוכיים על: He heard from residents and educational staff about daily life, hardships and challenges, and used this invaluable information to develop programs to narrow social gaps in Israel; he even read aloud in the Knesset a poem by Tuvia Solomi, a young poet and son of the neighborhood.
השכונה נתנה תקווה אינסופית גם למוזיקה הי: The neighborhood gave endless hope to Israeli music too. It produced cherished treasures such as Ofra Haza, Avner Gadassi, Dudu Tassa, the lyricist Yossi Gispan and the super-producers the Reuveni Brothers. The Israeli soundtrack that played in the neighborhood began with the liturgical poems (piyyutim) and choirs of the synagogues, and continued in the "Hatikva Neighborhood Theater" workshop, led by Bezalel Aloni and starring Ofra Haza and Michael Sinwani.
כמות הכישרון שיצאה משכונה כה קטנה מעוררת: The amount of talent that came out of such a small neighborhood is truly astonishing. The residents' love of music could be felt in the homes and courtyards, in the restaurants and the market, at Café Noah and in the Nadav halls. Today the neighborhood's melody carries on at the Dohal Theater and the Beit Dani community center, through careful nurturing of young talent.
שמם של האחים ראובני חקוק באותיות זהב בדב: The name of the Reuveni Brothers is engraved in golden letters in the annals of Israeli music. The cultural revolution they brought about is an inspiration for generations, worthy of the Israel Prize. There is hardly an article about a trailblazing figure in the history of Mizrahi music that does not pass through their legendary shop on Derech HaHagana opposite the market.
אשר ומאיר ראובני הקליטו כ- 700 אלבומים ו: Asher and Meir Reuveni recorded some 700 albums and produced musical giants such as Zohar Argov, Haim Moshe, Margalit (Margol), Ahuva Ozeri, Daklon, Shimi Tavori and Jackie Makaytan. Their productions were ahead of their time, and they had the vision to create groundbreaking collaborations with icons such as Uzi Hitman and Nancy Brandes.
האחים ראובני הם דוגמא ומופת לערך מרכזי ב: The Reuveni Brothers are a model of a central value in the history of the Hatikva neighborhood: visionary enterprise and action that turn impossible dreams into reality. They did not accept cultural exclusion and the closed walls of the playlist; they did not despair even when the records they brought to radio stations were found thrown in a pile by the bin.
הקשיים העצומים רק דרבנו אותם להתגבר על ה: The enormous difficulties only spurred them to overcome the obstacles in creative ways, such as recording a musical haflah at a wedding and spreading it far and wide, or recognizing the old Central Bus Station as an ideal platform for spreading their musical message, by distributing cassettes for sale to stall and shop owners. That message is the leading musical stream in Israel today – and no one is more responsible for it than the neighborhood's most famous brothers.

She won the title of Israel's Singer of the Year four times, Germany's Singer of the Year twice, and a special award at the Grammys in the world music category. Her "Im Nin'alu" is the best-selling Israeli hit ever worldwide, and many great artists around the world saw her as an inspiration.
בינואר 2023 נבחרה עפרה לאחת מ-200 הזמרות: In January 2023 Ofra was named one of the 200 greatest singers of all time in a ranking by the legendary culture magazine "Rolling Stone". גם בחייה גילמה עפרה את השילוב בין הישן ל: In her life, too, Ofra embodied the blend of old and new, local and global. She never forgot where she came from, even at the height of her international success, and always kept close ties with the neighborhood of her childhood, which she saw as a source of pride.
היא תמיד זכרה איך התחיל המסע שלה: בלהקה: She always remembered how her journey began: in the troupe of the Hatikva Neighborhood Theater workshop, which she joined as a girl, under the guidance of Bezalel Aloni and together with the singer Michael Sinwani. It was a trailblazing workshop that combined Mizrahi music with original, social theater, and laid the foundations for Ofra's unforgettable career.

האחים סאלח ודאוד אל-כוויתי, עיראקים שנול: The brothers Saleh and Daoud Al-Kuwaiti, Iraqis born in Kuwait who returned to Iraq following their musical success, are considered the founders of modern Iraqi music and two of the greatest artists of all time in the Arab world. They excelled on the oud and the violin and wrote more than 700 songs, including for famous singers such as Umm Kulthum and Salima Murad.
המעמד שלהם בעולם הערבי היה חסר תקדים: הם: Their status in the Arab world was unprecedented: they played at the coronation of the King of Iraq in 1935 and founded the Iraqi radio orchestra a year later. Before they immigrated to Israel in 1951, the then ruler of Kuwait sent diplomats who blocked the runway and tried to persuade the brothers to give up the move to Israel, fearing the damage their departure would do to the cultures of Iraq and Kuwait.
לאחר עלייתם ארצה השתקעו האחים אל-כוויתי: After immigrating, the Al-Kuwaiti brothers settled in the Hatikva neighborhood, played every Friday for the audience that filled Café Noah, and opened a housewares shop in Hatikva Market, which also served as the booking office for their performances. Although the two were given a weekly one-hour program on Kol Israel radio in Arabic, they did not receive the recognition that had accompanied them in their countries of origin, and so they forbade their children to study music.
לפחות חבר אחד במשפחה לא שעה לאיסור המדוב: At least one member of the family did not heed that ban: Daoud Al-Kuwaiti's grandson, Dudu Tassa, who has done much to commemorate their legacy, including recording an entire album of their songs. Thanks to Dudu's work, which expressed in deeds the value of tradition and heritage typical of the residents of Hatikva, the brothers won a special place in Israeli culture too – and a street in the neighborhood named after them.

גם בתרבות, השכונה תפקדה כמו עיר בפני עצמ: In culture too, the neighborhood functioned like a city of its own from its earliest years, with its own cinema, "Cinema Darom", the magnificent "Nadav Halls" that were home to the residents' celebrations and events, and "Café Noah", which bordered the neighborhood and was home to original Mizrahi and Arabic musical creation. These institutions joined many homes and initiatives within the neighborhood that hosted cultural gatherings of various kinds.
תנופה תרבותית נרשמה בשכונה עם הקמת מרכז: The neighborhood saw a cultural surge with the founding of the Dohal Center for the Performing Arts, the largest neighborhood theater in the city, inaugurated in 1986, which was joined in 1997 by the Yoram Levinstein Acting Studio, which moved into the historic Beit Hanna-Rovina in the heart of the market.

המשורר בן השכונה טוביה סולמי ביקש בשירו: The neighborhood poet Tuvia Solomi asked in his poem to tear open a window in his neighborhood's walls, to look out on all its colors. Since then many have answered his request and torn open a window in the walls of Hatikva to look out on its many colors. The number of works written about such a small neighborhood is truly staggering: poetry, prose, film, television, journalism, plays, stand-up, academic research, visual art, graffiti and even waltzes and dances inspired by it. Art is born when the soul overflows and tries to translate the elation it feels into a real work in the world, and that is certainly a feeling the neighborhood stirs in its residents and visitors.

שכונה שמבוססת על ערכים מציבה בראש מעייני: A neighborhood built on values puts education first. From its cradle, the neighborhood's leaders and residents understood the importance of founding educational institutions, which in their first form were learning frameworks inside the synagogues. In the 1950s official schools and a "Youth House" in Gan HaTikva were founded. In the 1970s a historic decision was made: to found the Beit Dani community center.
הבית נוסד בשנת 1979 והוא קרוי על שמו של: The house was founded in 1979 and is named after the late Danny Moshevitz, who was killed in a plane crash. Danny was the son of Marc Moshevitz, one of the owners of the "Elite" company. The Beit Dani compound, on land donated by the Tel Aviv municipality, is considered one of the most magnificent in Israel and covers 12 dunams. The community center serves on average some 5,000 residents every week, and its educational, social and cultural value can hardly be overstated. The dear Moshevitz family accompanies Beit Dani to this day.
בית דני הוא בית התקווה - הלב הפועם של הש: Beit Dani is the house of Hatikva – the beating heart of the neighborhood, a social lighthouse and a moral compass, open to every person from everywhere and of every age; a vision fulfilled as a center for the empowerment and flourishing of the individual as part of the community in which they are rooted. Tens of thousands of its graduates over the years testify that it is a house that changes lives, and some call it "our Temple". And indeed it is a temple of values, achievements and neighborhood pride.

גד סולמי, ממייסדי אגודת בני יהודה, ואחיו: Gad Solomi, one of the founders of the Bnei Yehuda association, and his brother David, the association's secretary, ran the club for decades. In their eyes Bnei Yehuda was not just a football team but an educational institution: a place that takes young people off the street, gives them a framework and pride, and accompanies them through school, the army and their bar mitzvah.
גד גדל בשכונה בתקופת המנדט, ובנעוריו נעצ: Gad grew up in the neighborhood during the Mandate, and as a youth was arrested by the British in an underground operation. When he returned, he devoted his life to the neighborhood's youth.
\"אנו אגודת בני יהודה, שמנו לעצמנו למטרה: "We, the Bnei Yehuda association, have set ourselves the goal of caring for the physical and mental health of our neighborhood's youth"
באוגוסט 1947 נעצר ביפו כשהוא מחופש לערבי: In August 1947 he was arrested in Jaffa disguised as an Arab, leading a camel loaded with mines. According to "Haaretz", he refused to recognize the authority of the military court and was sentenced to 15 years in prison. According to the family's account he was first sentenced to death, commuted because of his age. He was released when the British left the country.
גד היה ממייסדי אגודת בני יהודה ועמד בראש: Gad was one of the founders of the Bnei Yehuda association and headed it, and David served as its secretary. The two ran the club for decades from an office at 25 Rishon LeZion St.
1961: מכתב לשר החינוך: 1961: a letter to the Minister of Education
ביוני 1961 כתב ועד בני יהודה לשר החינוך: In June 1961 the Bnei Yehuda committee wrote to Minister of Education Abba Eban: many of the young people "gather in groups in the street by the cafés and the cinema and waste their time", and "the only brake holding back the decline of the youth is sport". The committee asked for a budget "so that we may succeed in strengthening the physical fitness of the neighborhood's youth".
באותה שנה ביקש גד סולמי, כיו״ר האגודה, מ: That same year Gad Solomi, as chairman of the association, asked the Ministry of Education for a scholarship for a young player from a struggling family so he could study at the Wingate Institute: "Pay attention to this youth before it is abandoned and forsaken."
\"בני יהודה היא אגודה המייצגת שכונה שלמה: "Bnei Yehuda is an association that represents an entire neighborhood," said Mayor Shlomo Lahat in 1980. That evening David Solomi announced that because of "the educational mission" the association would double its youth and children's teams to eight and take in dozens of children.
מ־1979 אימצה \"עלית\" את בני יהודה. ב־19: From 1979 "Elite" adopted Bnei Yehuda. In 1984 the team, together with "Elite", held a joint bar mitzvah celebration for 19 boys from the neighborhood.
דוד סולמי היה מזכיר האגודה שעמד מול בית\: David Solomi was the association's secretary who stood up to Beitar Jerusalem in the Ehud Ben Tovim affair, and refused to be the first to write the request letter until Beitar gave up in writing.
תחת הנהגת האחים זכתה בני יהודה באליפות ה: Under the brothers' leadership Bnei Yehuda won the only national championship in its history.
\"הבלם היחידי העוצר בעד התדרדרות הנוער\": "The only brake holding back the decline of the youth"
המכתב לשר החינוך מ־18.6.1961 הוא האני מא: The letter to the Minister of Education of 18.6.1961 is Bnei Yehuda's credo: a sports association that defines itself as responsible "for the physical and mental health of our neighborhood's youth", that is "far from party politics and disputes", and that sees itself as "a force for peace and calm".
הטקסט מתאר שכונה צפופה שתושביה עובדים בע: The text describes a crowded neighborhood whose residents work with their hands and sometimes "cannot meet their families' needs and care for their children". The association steps into that gap. It does not wait for the state: it writes to the minister, asks for scholarships, and takes care of the young people itself.
זו אותה תפיסה שתחזור בבית דני ובוועד של: It is the same outlook that would return at Beit Dani and in Adina Nadiv's committee: do it ourselves, because there is no choice, and put education before everything.
מה ההבדל בין קבוצה שמנצחת לבין קבוצה שמח: What is the difference between a team that wins and a team that educates? Can it be both?

אהוד בן טובים נולד ב־12 באוגוסט 1952 וגד: Ehud Ben Tovim was born on 12 August 1952 and grew up at Bnei Yehuda. He played for the senior team for twenty seasons, from 1969 to 1989, and is considered the greatest talent the club ever produced.
הסיפור שלו הוא גם סיפור של שכונה שרואה ב: His story is also the story of a neighborhood that sees its player as part of the family – so much so that in the autumn of 1979 it took to the streets to prevent him from leaving, and the affair reached the office of the Deputy Prime Minister.
\"בשום מקום לא ארגיש כמו בשכונת התקווה,: "Nowhere will I feel as I do in the Hatikva neighborhood, my warm home – not at Maccabi Tel Aviv, and not at Liverpool either"
גדל במועדון של השכונה, שנוסד ב־1936 כאגו: He grew up in the neighborhood club, founded in 1936 as a sports association of young Yemenites, and moved up to the senior team in 1969.
445 הופעות ליגה ו־166 שערים במדי בני יהו: 445 league appearances and 166 goals in the Bnei Yehuda shirt. In the 1978 season he was loaned to the Oakland Stompers in the United States.
Two appearances for the national team in 1978.
After the 1978/79 season he asked for a raise and was turned down. He almost moved to Hapoel Be'er Sheva, and then Beitar Jerusalem closed a deal with Bnei Yehuda for 700,000 lira.
באוקטובר 1979 הבעירו אוהדים ותושבים צמיג: In October 1979 fans and residents set tires on fire, stopped public transport and demonstrated for days on end. The Deputy Prime Minister, Prof. Yigael Yadin, intervened, and a meeting on the affair was held in his office.
בן טובים פנה ליו״ר בית\"ר, עמוס אהרוני,: Ben Tovim turned to Beitar chairman Amos Aharoni and asked to be released. According to Aharoni, stones were thrown at his parents' house, and "he is not willing for people to be killed because of his move to the capital". He gave up the financial future he had been promised, and the neighborhood celebrated "the return of the king".
שיחק בשכונה עוד עשור, ועזב ב־1989, עונה: He played in the neighborhood for another decade and left in 1989, one season before the first and only championship in the club's history.
אחרי שנים של נתק וכאב מונה ב־2006 למאמן: After years of estrangement and pain he was appointed coach of Bnei Yehuda's youth team in 2006. In 2021 Kan 11 broadcast the film "The King Stayed in the Neighborhood" about the affair.
באוקטובר 1979 קיבלה השכונה החלטה במקום ה: In October 1979 the neighborhood made a decision in place of its player. The demonstrations closed roads and went on for days, fans threatened Beitar's management, and the neighborhood raised money to buy him back. The affair reached the office of Deputy Prime Minister Yigael Yadin. In the end Ben Tovim himself asked to be released, because he did not want people to be hurt on his account.
זה רגע של אהבה ושל בעלות: המועדון הוא של: It is a moment of love and of ownership: the club belongs to the residents, and the player is "theirs". But it is also a moment with a price. Decades later, the film about the affair describes a pain and a sense of loss that never healed.
המשפט שלו בחוברת, \"בשום מקום לא ארגיש כ: His sentence in the booklet, "Nowhere will I feel as I do in the Hatikva neighborhood", sounds like acceptance. It can also be read as a choice made slowly, after the decision had already been made for him.
האוהדים שניהלו את המשא ומתן אמרו שצריך ל: The fans who conducted the negotiations said he had to be brought back "to prevent bloodshed and for the good of the neighborhood". What does this say about the power of neighborhood identity, for better and for worse?
מתי אהבה של קהילה הופכת לכלוב? והאם היה: When does a community's love become a cage? And should they have let him leave?
הנאמנות שלו לשכונה עלתה לו בכסף ובקריירה: His loyalty to the neighborhood cost him money and his career. Would you have chosen as he did?
מי ב\"שכונה\" שלכם נשאר בשבילכם, ומה זה: Who in your "neighborhood" stayed for your sake, and what did it cost them?

מרק מושביץ (Marks Mosevics) נולד ב־22 בא: Marc Moshevitz (Marks Mosevics) was born on 22 August 1920 in Rostov, came to the Land of Israel from Riga during the war years, and in 1944 received Palestinian citizenship. Already then he was deputy manager of the "Elite" company, and later he became one of its owners and president of the Manufacturers' Association.
הוא לא גר בשכונת התקווה. הקשר שלו אליה נ: He did not live in the Hatikva neighborhood. His connection to it was born of tragedy: his son Danny, a pilot, was killed in 1971 when a light plane crashed near Herzliya. The father chose to commemorate him with a house for the neighborhood's young people.
\"הצעתי להקים בשכונת התקווה בית נוער צנו: "I proposed to build a modest youth house in the Hatikva neighborhood. I saw a need to help the neighborhood's young people"
נולד ב־1920 ברוסטוב, ונשא דרכון לטבי. הג: Born in 1920 in Rostov, he held a Latvian passport. He came to the country in 1940.
ב־1944 הוא כבר סגן מנהל ב\"עלית\". באותה: By 1944 he was already deputy manager at "Elite". That year his son Daniel was born in Tel Aviv, and the family received citizenship.
נשיא התאחדות בעלי התעשייה, ונשיא כבוד של: President of the Manufacturers' Association, and honorary president of "Akim", the association for people with intellectual disabilities.
דני מושביץ נהרג בהתרסקות מטוס \"ססנה\" ב: Danny Moshevitz was killed when a "Cessna" plane crashed at the airfield near Herzliya.
בלשכת שר האוצר נחתם הסכם בין הממשלה, עיר: In the Finance Minister's office an agreement was signed between the government, the Tel Aviv municipality, the Moshevitz family and "Elite" to build a community center named after Danny. The cost: 5 million lira, half from the family and "Elite" and half from the state. The municipality donated the land.
בית דני נחנך במאי 1979. \"לא סופרמרקט של: Beit Dani was inaugurated in May 1979. "Not a supermarket of activity groups," said director Yossi Cohen, "but a place to lay the foundations of good citizenship for the neighborhood's young people."
אחרי שבית דני קם, פנה ראש העיר שלמה (צ׳י: After Beit Dani was built, Mayor Shlomo (Chich) Lahat turned to the people of "Elite": "You must continue in this direction and take Bnei Yehuda under your wing too." "Elite" adopted the team, "not only for advertising purposes, but also through real involvement and activity". At first the neighborhood did not believe it, but "Elite" CEO Avi Filosof came to the games for years, sat on the board and became "chairman of the football department".
משפחת מושביץ מלווה את בית דני כבר יותר מ: The Moshevitz family has accompanied Beit Dani for more than 45 years. Beit Dani also has a dance studio named after Gabi Moshevitz.
בכתבה ב\"מעריב\" ביום החנוכה, 25.5.1979,: In an article in "Maariv" on the day of the inauguration, 25.5.1979, Moshevitz explains that he approached Finance Minister Pinhas Sapir on his own initiative, because "Danny too was very aware of social problems and of the problems of young people wandering the streets with nowhere to go".
זו נתינה במובן העמוק: אדם מחוץ לשכונה, ש: This is giving in the deepest sense: a man from outside the neighborhood, who owed it nothing, turns his private grief into a place that serves thousands of families every week. The house born of death became "the beating heart of the neighborhood".
מכאן נמשך הקשר גם לכדורגל. בראיון ל\"מער: From here the connection extended to football too. In an interview with "Maariv" in 1989, Avi Filosof, who actually grew up a Maccabi Tel Aviv fan, said the sponsorship of Bnei Yehuda was born of Beit Dani: when the team is up top it is "a focus of identification and imitation that brings a lot of children into a framework", and if it goes down there will be "a lot of children in the street instead of at Beit Dani". He added: "When a person becomes established in life, he should give back 10 percent of his time to the community."
גם אהוד בן טובים אמר ב־1983, בעונה קשה:: Ehud Ben Tovim also said in 1983, in a difficult season: "There is one bright spot. Avi Filosof, one of the heads of the Elite concern, who adopts the team. Without him we'd be finished."
החיבור בין העשייה של מושביץ לבין הדרישה: The link between Moshevitz's deeds and Adina Nadiv's demand, "Before you raise a building, raise the spirit of the person", is exactly what made Beit Dani more than a building.
מה ההבדל בין תורם שבא \"לעזור לשכונה\" ל: What is the difference between a donor who comes "to help the neighborhood" and a donor who builds with it? How did Beit Dani manage to turn from a donation into a home?
איך אפשר להפוך אובדן פרטי לעשייה ציבורית: How can a private loss be turned into public action? Are there such examples in your own family?
אם הייתם מקימים מקום בשכונה לזכר מישהו,: If you were to create a place in the neighborhood in someone's memory, what would it be?
\"מרכז קהילתי ע״ש דן מושביץ יוקם בשכונת: "A community center named after Dan Moshevitz will be built in the Hatikva neighborhood"

בת שבע עפרה חזה נולדה ב־19 בנובמבר 1957: Bat-Sheva Ofra Haza was born on 19 November 1957 in the Hatikva neighborhood, the youngest in a large family of immigrants from Yemen. The family home stood at 39 Boaz St.
כנערה הצטרפה לסדנת תיאטרון שכונת התקווה: As a girl she joined Bezalel Aloni's Hatikva Neighborhood Theater workshop; he recognized her talent and became her manager. From the neighborhood workshop a road opened that led to the Eurovision, Germany, Japan and the charts in the United States.
\"גם בשיא הצלחתה הבינלאומית לא שכחה את ה: "Even at the height of her international success she did not forget where she came from"
ילדות בבית תימני מסורתי, עם פיוטים ושירי: A childhood in a traditional Yemenite home, with piyyutim and women's songs, in a neighborhood where music was heard from the synagogues, the courtyards and the market.
סדנת תיאטרון שכונת התקווה, בהדרכת בצלאל: The Hatikva Neighborhood Theater workshop, guided by Bezalel Aloni and alongside Michael Sinwani, combined Mizrahi music with original social theater. That is where the road began.
בסוף שנות ה־70 ובתחילת שנות ה־80 הפכה לא: In the late 1970s and early 1980s she became one of the country's best-loved singers, and won the title of Singer of the Year four times.
במינכן שרה את \"חי\" (\"עם ישראל חי\") ש: In Munich she sang "Chai" ("Am Yisrael Chai") by Ehud Manor and Avi Toledano, and came second.
שירי המסורת שגדלה עליהם, ובראשם \"אם ננע: The traditional songs she grew up on, above all "Im Nin'alu", became international hits in modern arrangements. She was named Singer of the Year in Germany and won a Grammy nomination.
שמרה על קשר הדוק עם הוריה ועם שכנים, חזר: She kept close ties with her parents and neighbors, came back to visit and perform, and presented Hatikva as a source of pride.
נפטרה ב־23 בפברואר 2000, בגיל 42. ב־2023: She died on 23 February 2000, aged 42. In 2023 she was included in Rolling Stone's list of the 200 greatest singers of all time.
\"ידעה לשלב את היותה בת השכונה\": "She knew how to combine being a daughter of the neighborhood"
עמוד החוברת מציג את עפרה בבית המשפחה ברח: The booklet page shows Ofra in the family home on Boaz St., with her mother and father, in a traditional Yemenite dress and in a star's clothes. That combination is the point: she did not have to choose between the worlds.
\"רולינג סטון\" כתב שחזה שילבה ווקאליות: "Rolling Stone" wrote that Haza blended traditional vocals with modern technique to create something that sounds ancient and ahead of its time at the same time. It is also a good description of the neighborhood itself.
בלי סדנת התיאטרון השכונתית, האם הכישרון: Without the neighborhood theater workshop, would the talent have been discovered? What is the equivalent of that workshop in the neighborhood today?
הדבר שנחשב אז \"שכונתי\" ו\"עדתי\", שירי: What was then considered "neighborhood" and "ethnic" – Yemenite songs – is exactly what conquered the world. What does that say about shame and about pride?
איזה שיר מהבית שלכם הייתם רוצים שהעולם י: Which song from your home would you like the world to hear?

היא נולדה בדמשק למשפחה אמידה ומכובדת, על: She was born in Damascus to a wealthy and respected family, immigrated as a girl in a group of young women recruited by Rachel Yanait Ben-Zvi, passed through a women workers' farm, kibbutzim and the Palmach, and came to the Hatikva neighborhood. Here she became one of the strongest neighborhood leaders in the country.
היא הקימה ועד פתוח לכל התושבים, עמדה מול: She founded a committee open to all residents, stood up to the government, the municipality and the American donors, and insisted that renewal begin with the person and not with the building.
\"לפני שאתם מרימים בניין, תרימו את נפשו: "Before you raise a building, raise the spirit of the person"
מדמשק לוועד השכונה: From Damascus to the neighborhood committee
התחנות מבוססות על ראיון עומק שנתנה ב־199: The stations are based on an in-depth interview she gave in 1999 to a project documenting immigration from Syria and Lebanon. They are presented as she told them, in her own voice.
בתו של אליהו אינדיבו־כהן, מהסוחרים הגדול: Daughter of Eliyahu Indibo-Cohen, one of the great merchants of Syria, and of Frida, who was active in community life. Her uncle, Rabbi Nissim Indibo-Cohen, was head of the rabbinical court. She studied at the "Alliance" school in Hebrew, French and Arabic.
רחל ינאית בן־צבי הגיעה לדמשק לגייס בנות: Rachel Yanait Ben-Zvi came to Damascus to recruit girls for immigration, and the community leaders advised her to start with the wealthy families. She stayed at the family home and spoke in the "Alliance" classrooms, and when the authorities sought to arrest her, the father hid her in his house and smuggled her back to the Land of Israel.
האב הוציא דרכונים לכל בנות הקבוצה. הן נס: The father obtained passports for all the girls in the group. They traveled by bus through Beirut and Rosh HaNikra, as "students coming to study agriculture", and reached the immigrants' house in Haifa. "They gave us black bread with jam to eat."
משק הפועלות בפתח תקווה: The women workers' farm in Petah Tikva
בית ספר חקלאי של מועצת הפועלות: עבודה בב: An agricultural school of the Women Workers' Council: work in the morning, studies in the afternoon. Girls who had grown up with servants were required to milk cows and clean chicken coops, and demanded "give us our suitcases". Her mother came to visit, was shocked by the shorts, and was persuaded to leave her daughters there.
אשדות יעקב, יגור עם \"הקבוצה התורכית\" ו: Ashdot Yaakov, Yagur with "the Turkish group", and Sde Nahum, as part of Youth Aliyah. In the War of Independence she escorted convoys with the Palmach, and later served in the Givati brigade.
הקיבוץ שלח אותה לפעילות בחירות בשכונה, ו: The kibbutz sent her to do election work in the neighborhood, and she stayed in the city. After a while she left Ahdut HaAvoda with a large group for Mapam, "because of the glaring discrimination", and worked for many years as a party "social worker", from person to person.
בסוף שנות ה־70 בחרו בה התושבים לייצג אות: In the late 1970s the residents chose her to represent them before the Neighborhood Renewal Project and New York Jewry. She headed the neighborhood committee and built the model of the open committee and residents' representation on the steering committee.
אחרי מלחמת ששת הימים התקרבה למסורת, \"את: After the Six-Day War she drew closer to tradition – "you need to go back to the roots" – and remained active in Mapam as a Sabbath observer. In her last years she gave lectures on Judaism to the neighborhood's elderly and was active in women's charity groups.
הכרזה הצהובה של ועד שכונת התקווה: The yellow poster of the Hatikva neighborhood committee
\"תושב/תושבת שכ׳ התקוה יקרים!\" · לחצו ל: "Dear residents of the Hatikva neighborhood!" · click to enlarge
הכרזה הצהובה: \"אל תגררו להפגנות אלימות!: The yellow poster: "Do not be drawn into violent demonstrations!"
הכרזה יצאה מ\"ועד שכונת התקוה, רחוב ההגנ: The poster was issued by "the Hatikva Neighborhood Committee, 61 Derech HaHagana", the same address and phone number that appear on the letters Adina Nadiv signed as chair of the committee. It was written at a time when distressed neighborhoods all over the country took to the streets in stormy protests, and the committee chose a different path.
\"יש לנו את בית־דני בשכונה ולא צעקנו 'על: "We have Beit Dani in the neighborhood and we didn't shout 'charge!' to get it"
היא מונה הישגים ולא מצוקות: מחשבים בבתי: It lists achievements, not hardships: computers in the schools, a long school day, after-school clubs, house renovations and Beit Dani.
אחרי כל הישג חוזר המשפט \"ולא שרפנו צמיג: After each achievement the sentence returns: "and we didn't burn tires to get it". In this way it turns the achievement itself into an argument against violence.
היא פונה לתושב ולתושבת כשותפים: הכבוד של: It addresses each resident, man and woman, as a partner: the neighborhood's honor depends on them, not only on the institutions.
זהו מסמך של שינוי תדמית מבפנים. במקום לב: This is a document of image change from within. Instead of asking the world to see the neighborhood differently, the committee asks the residents to be the proof of it. This is exactly the outlook Adina described: "not to ask, but to come and contribute, and only then to ask".
באותה רוח פנה הוועד ב־16.4.1981 ליועץ המ: In the same spirit, on 16.4.1981 the committee wrote to the Attorney General, Yitzhak Zamir, against an article in "Yedioth Ahronoth" that portrayed the residents as criminals, and sent copies to President Navon and Prime Minister Begin. The struggle over the image was fought on two fronts: against the media, with the tools of the law, and among the residents, with the tools of pride.
המהפכה בניהול השכונה: The Revolution in Running the Neighborhood
בסוף שנות ה־70 הגיעו לשכונה נציגי הסוכנו: In the late 1970s representatives of the Jewish Agency, Keren Hayesod and New York Jewry came to the neighborhood as part of the Neighborhood Renewal Project. "They said: we've come to build, we've come to fix." Her answer became the neighborhood's motto:
\"לפני שאתם הולכים להרים בנין, תרימו את: "Before you go and raise a building, raise the spirit of the person. Then build the building"
היא התנתה את שיתוף הפעולה בסדר עדיפויות:: She made cooperation conditional on an order of priorities: education, welfare, employment, the fight against drugs and crime, and only then housing. According to her, when the representatives presented this to Prime Minister Menachem Begin, he said: "Bless you! That is the purpose of Neighborhood Renewal."
\"אני פתחתי את הוועד לכל התושבים\". בכל: "I opened the committee to all the residents." Every Friday a committee meeting open to the whole community convened, and anyone who wanted brought their problem. "Not to ask, but to come and contribute, and only then to ask. First of all, give of yourself. Not money, but of your abilities."
מתוך הוועד הרחב נבחרו נציגים לוועדת ההיג: From the broad committee, representatives were elected to the Neighborhood Renewal steering committee. On it sat government representatives and, facing them "with equal power", the residents' representatives.
\"שום דבר לא נחתם בלי שיקבל את האוקיי של: "Nothing was signed without the okay of my steering committee and of the parents' committee in the schools." The same in education and welfare: the teacher, the principal and the parents' representative sat together and approved the plan.
קרן היסוד והאמריקאים הציעו לה משכורת כפו: Keren Hayesod and the Americans offered her a double salary. She refused: "If I was elected as the neighborhood's representative, I want to tell the prime minister what I think and the municipality what I think, and not depend on a salary from you or from him."
מודל לארץ כולה: A model for the whole country
לדבריה המודל שצמח בשכונה הועתק לשכונות א: According to her, the model that grew in the neighborhood was copied to other neighborhoods, and in the end she represented all the neighborhoods in the country.
מתוך המודל הזה צמחו דברים שעומדים בשכונה: From this model grew things that stand in the neighborhood to this day: replacing teachers and principals in the schools together with the Ministry of Education, kindergartens and day-care centers, tackling the drug problem, and Beit Dani with the Beit Dohal theater, the sports hall and the swimming pool.
קריאה ביקורתית: כמה דברים לחשוב עליהם: A Critical Reading: Some Things to Think About
הנערה שבאה מבית עם משרתות ונדרשה לחלוב פ: The girl who came from a home with servants and had to milk cows is the same woman who demanded of the neighborhood "give of yourself". The story can be read as a path of growing up: from receiving service to giving it.

את שכונת התקווה מכירים רבים דרך הבטן ודר: Many people know the Hatikva neighborhood through their stomachs and their ears. Family businesses that started as a small stall or a shop of a few meters became institutions: Yemenite soup cooked in the same pot for two generations, Iraqi kubbeh, spices that went from the market to the whole country, a bakery that opened by chance, and a café where Eastern music played before the radio gave it a place. Each is a story of immigration, family and hard work – and of loyalty to the neighborhood.

בתי הכנסת של שכונת התקווה: The Synagogues of the Hatikva Neighborhood
20 בתי כנסת מההקמה ועד שנות ה־50: הכתובו: 20 synagogues from the founding to the 1950s: the addresses, the communities, the prayer rites and the stories
At its peak the neighborhood had some 130 active synagogues. Every community and every large family founded its own "house of prayer": immigrants from Yemen, Aleppo, Turkey, Iraq, Persia, Bukhara, Afghanistan and Ashkenazi lands. Many still operate today in small houses on the neighborhood's streets, and many others are no longer active. Documented here are 20 of them, with the address, the year of founding, the community and the prayer rite. Click a synagogue for photographs, its story and navigation.

בית הכנסת ממוקם במבנה חד קומתי (בגובה 'כ: The synagogue is housed in a single-story building (with a "double-height" hall) in the eastern part of the neighborhood. The building has a tiled roof and includes restrooms and adjoining spaces.
חלל בית הכנסת מלבני. אורכו (ממזרח למערב): The prayer hall is rectangular. Its length (east to west) is about 10.5 m and its width (north to south) about 7.5 m (an area of about 80 m²). The entrance is from the western façade, facing the street. The women's section is in a gallery running along the western façade only, reached by an open outdoor staircase. The gallery is supported by two columns that mark the boundary between the entrance space and the prayer hall. The columns bear the inscriptions: "Blessed are you when you come in", "Blessed are you when you go out".

צוואה מוסרית בשלושה עמודים. הוא פותח במו: A moral testament in three pages. He opens with death ("Honored children, know that the end of man is to die") and with the question of how one leaves a good name. Then comes a long list of instructions in a fixed structure: "Please…" followed by "and fulfill…" and a verse. Among them: humility, truth, avoiding slander, honoring one's wife, a friend's property, moderation, the Sabbath. The ending is national: "and Israel shall dwell securely in its land". He signs "the faithful mohel, devoted to you all".
המסמך המכונן של הרב אבדר. הוא כתוב לפי פ: Rabbi Avdar's foundational document. It is written as an address to "the Children of Israel" rather than "the People of Israel": a fatherly address, from one who brought generations of the neighborhood's children into the covenant of Abraham. The blessing "may you be sealed for good" shows it was written during the Ten Days of Repentance.
הנני פונה בקריאה נרגשת לבני ישראל: I hereby address a heartfelt call to the Children of Israel
בניים נכבדים, דעו כי סוף אדם למות. מי גב: Honored children, know that the end of man is to die. What man shall live and not see death? And if so, it is your duty to think about what is done on the face of the earth, and to consider which path to take so that a person will have a good name in life and after his long days […]. And so, please refrain from doing evil, both to oneself and to others; only do good to every human being, and be content with what God has granted us, even if it is little. And if it is much – it is said: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches", for all is vanity, and they leave their wealth to others.
נא להתרחק מן המריבות והקנאה והשנאה. נא ל: Please keep away from quarrels, envy and hatred. Please keep away from lies and pursue truth and justice. Please keep away from slander and gossip, and do not accept them. Please do not befriend a person unless you know him by his purse, his anger and his cup. Please do not harm any human being, and fulfill "Love your neighbor as yourself". Please honor your parents, and fulfill "Honor your father and your mother". Beware of slighting your God, and fulfill "Honor the Lord with your substance". Take care of your wife's honor and guard her like the apple of your eye, for blessing will then reign in your home. Do not reveal your secret, and guard your mouth and your tongue from all evil.
נא להתרחק מהגאווה, והנהג עצמך במידת הענו: Please keep away from pride, and conduct yourself with humility and reverence. Please keep away from anger and all foul language, and accustom yourself to speak pleasantly with every human being. Please do not hurry to answer those who insult you; weigh your words before you speak, and honor will come in the end. Please beware of every evil thing and do not bring it into your home, lest it destroy your home. Please let your friend's property be as dear to you as your own, and fulfill "You shall not covet your neighbor's house". Please do not deceive your friend nor take his money, and fulfill the commandment "You shall not steal", lest you stumble and be ashamed.
נא ליהנות מיגיע כפיך ואפילו מעט, כי אתה: Please enjoy the labor of your hands, even if it is little, for you are greater than one who fears Heaven. "Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider her ways and be wise." Please enjoy every food the Torah has permitted you, and beware of every food the Torah has forbidden, and fulfill "Take good heed unto yourselves". Please do not overindulge in food and drink; eat to be satisfied, give thanks and be blessed, for the end of man is worm and maggot. Please guard the Sabbath well, and fulfill "and He rested on the seventh day", and be blessed with the blessing of the seventh day […]. Please do not hurry to run to evil, and keep your foot from going; sit in your home and rejoice with the wife of your youth and your family. By the merit of keeping the Sabbath, God will bless your savings and provide for you, and bless the work of your hands.
נא שמור מאוד על הערכים – השבת ומוסר ישרא: Please guard the values well – the Sabbath and the morals of Israel.
[…] הקדושים אשר בזכותם הגענו עד הלום, וה: […] the holy ones by whose merit we have come this far, and the verse has been fulfilled in us: "I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you unto Myself." Every man under his vine and under his fig tree. "Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more", and Israel shall dwell securely in its land. And may your rest be full of joy and gladness, amen. And I conclude with feelings of respect for you all: may you be sealed for good.

\"המוהל הנאמן\": קריאה בכתביו של הרב שלו: "The Faithful Mohel": A Reading of the Writings of Rabbi Shalom Avdar
ארבעה כתבי יד, מסע של עשור מתימן דרך המז: Four manuscripts, a decade-long journey from Yemen through the Far East to the Hatikva neighborhood, and a whole life of service. Where the text is open, several possible readings are presented. There is no single correct interpretation here. The questions invite every reader to consider how the words meet them and their family.
2. המספר כגיבור: \"קמתי ועשיתי\": 2. The narrator as hero: "I rose and did"
3. המסע: מתימן דרך המזרח הרחוק לשכונת הת: 3. The journey: from Yemen through the Far East to the Hatikva neighborhood
4. הלשון: פסוק, דוח ותוכחה: 4. The language: verse, report and rebuke
5. מה שהטקסטים לא אומרים: 5. What the texts do not say
