7. הערכים ושרידותה של שכונת התקווה: 7. The values and the survival of the Hatikva neighborhood
בארכיון נשמרו ארבעה כתבים בכתב ידו, וכל: Four writings in his hand survive in the archive, each belonging to a different genre. "The story of his life" is a first-person travel memoir. "The history of the Hatikva neighborhood" is a community chronicle in which he writes about himself in the third person ("Rabbi Avdar immigrated to the Land"). The letter to his sons and grandchildren is a family blessing written on Tu BiShvat. "The heartfelt call to the Children of Israel" is a moral testament written during the High Holy Days.
למרות ההבדלים, הקול אחד. כמעט כל טקסט נג: Despite the differences, the voice is one. Almost every text ends with the same movement: from the personal story to the moral instruction, and from the home to the people. His favorite biblical quotations recur too, such as "The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine", "Love your neighbor as yourself" and "Be strong and of good courage". Even when he tells about himself, he is really teaching.
איזו מהסוגות קרובה אליכם: הסיפור, הכרוני: Which of the genres is closest to you: the story, the chronicle, the blessing or the testament? And in which would you write to your grandchildren?
המספר כגיבור: \"קמתי ועשיתי\": The Narrator as Hero: "I Rose and Did"
In the story of his life the rabbi is almost always the one who takes the initiative. He "rose and wrote two letters" to the Mizrachi Organization and the Histadrut so they would open a school in the neighborhood. Within a week he "counted" the children who were not in school. With two others he signed the document annexing the neighborhood to Tel Aviv. After the failures – in Shanghai, Rangoon, Calcutta and Damascus – he does not break. He simply moves on to the next station.
קורא ביקורתי ישים לב שהמספרים והתאריכים: A critical reader will notice that the numbers and dates do not always agree. In the story of his life he counted "more than 5,000 children", and in the history of the neighborhood "close to 3,500". The year of his immigration appears as 1936, 1938, 1939 and 1940. The chronicle resolves part of the gap: he arrived in 1936, went back to Lebanon and settled for good in 1939.
קריאה ראשונה: זיכרון שמעצב מורשת: First reading: memory that shapes heritage
אדם מבוגר כותב בשנות ה־80 על אירועים מלפ: An elderly man writes in the 1980s about events 40–50 years earlier. He enlarges his own part, like most memoirists, so that the story will carry the values he wishes to pass on.
קריאה שנייה: עדות של מנהיג בפועל: Second reading: the testimony of a leader in action
התעודות שבארכיון תומכות בשלד הסיפור: ההמ: The certificates in the archive support the skeleton of the story: the recommendations from Peshawar, Beirut and Tel Aviv, and the three professions. There is no reason to doubt that he did indeed initiate and act. The exact numbers matter less than the fact that someone rose and acted.
\"שלושתנו חתמנו\", \"פתחנו\", \"התארגנו: "The three of us signed", "we opened", "we organized and founded a committee". His "I" is always part of a group. His leadership can be read as public service rather than pride. Indeed, he himself warns in his testament: "Please keep away from pride."
כשאתם מספרים את סיפור המשפחה שלכם, מי הו: When you tell your family's story, who is the hero? And what happens to the story when it is told in the third person?
המסע: מתימן דרך המזרח הרחוק לשכונת התקוו: The Journey: From Yemen Through the Far East to the Hatikva Neighborhood
החלק המפתיע ביותר בסיפור הוא המסע. ב־192: The most surprising part of the story is the journey. In 1928 he left Yemen through Aden. At the first station, apparently Singapore, he learned within a month to read with Sephardi pronunciation, to serve a community not his own. From there he went on to Shanghai, Hong Kong, Rangoon, Calcutta and Bombay, where he opened a heder for Torah study. From there the community of Bukharan Jews in Peshawar invited him, and he served there for more than three years. Members of the community, who had houses in Jerusalem, "praised the Land of Israel before him", and so the desire to immigrate was born.
בדרך לארץ, ב־1936, ניסה לעבור דרך בגדאד: On his way to the Land, in 1936, he tried to pass through Baghdad and Damascus but was stuck because of the riots. He sat in Damascus for three months without work, then went on to Beirut. There he was examined in the laws of ritual slaughter and got a post. Only in 1939 did he reach Rehovot, and from there the Hatikva neighborhood.
וחשוב מכל: עוד לפני שעלה בעצמו, כשעבד בפ: And most important of all: even before he immigrated himself, while working in Peshawar, he funded the immigration of his entire father's house, "15 souls in number", who reached Rehovot in 1933.
המסע כבית ספר לקבלת האחר: The journey as a school for accepting the other
הוא שירת יהודים מתימן, מבוכרה, מלבנון ומ: He served Jews from Yemen, from Bukhara, from Lebanon and from the Sephardi community in Tel Aviv, and learned all their customs. Perhaps this is the source of his ability to connect communities in the neighborhood.
אפשר לקרוא את הסיפור גם בלי רומנטיקה: אד: The story can also be read without romance: a young man looking for work, failing and trying again. The values grow out of the hardship, not before it.
מאילו תחנות הגיעה המשפחה שלכם? מה כל תחנ: From which stations did your family come? What did each station teach it?
הלשון: פסוק, דוח ותוכחה: The Language: Verse, Report and Rebuke
העברית שלו היא שכבות על שכבות. יש בה לשו: His Hebrew is layer upon layer. It has the language of the Bible and the prayer book alongside modern public language: "census", "Histadrut", "inflation", "supermarkets". In the testament he builds a fixed pattern: "Please…" followed by "and fulfill…" and a verse. Every moral instruction is tied to a commandment, and morality becomes part of religion itself.
בכתבים המאוחרים חוזר גם סיפור של \"ירידת: The later writings also repeat a story of "the decline of the generations". Once "they did not steal or cheat or rob, and lived lives of modesty and honor". Today there is television, crime, young people who leave, and synagogues searching for a minyan.
זה מוטיב מוכר בכרוניקות קהילתיות. העבר מ: This is a familiar motif in community chronicles. The past grows more beautiful. Indeed, in the writings themselves he describes poverty, swamps and floods "a meter high" in the years 1940–1956.
הוא לא מאשים רק את הנוער. הוא מאשים במפו: He does not blame only the young. He explicitly blames the government and the construction companies "who make fortunes at the people's expense", and demands that the state build apartments at reasonable prices. It is a voice of social justice, resting on the language of the prophets and the laws of the Jubilee.
מבחינתו, המשבר הוא משבר של חינוך: \"צמא: For him the crisis is a crisis of education: "a thirst for Torah and morals, a thirst for religious guidance". He criticizes the school curriculum, and here present-day readers may disagree with him.
האם המשבר שתיאר ב־1985 מוכר לכם היום? מה: Is the crisis he described in 1985 familiar to you today? What in his words would you adopt, and what would you argue with him about?
מה שהטקסטים לא אומרים: What the Texts Do Not Say
קריאה ביקורתית שמה לב גם לשתיקות. הרבנית: A critical reading also notices the silences. Rabbanit Saada Mazal, his wife, appears in the writings mainly as the one who "stayed in her parents' home" and as one who must be "guarded like the apple of your eye". But according to the preserved tradition – as is also written on the heritage wall – the couple were known for the kindness they did together. Bereavement too – the deaths of his son Ovadia and his daughter-in-law Tziona – is not mentioned in the writings we have. Sons were born to him in Lebanon, and a family of 11 children remains in the background.
הסגנון של דורו: כבוד לאישה ולמשפחה, וצני: The style of his generation: respect for one's wife and family, and a modesty that does not tell about the home.
אולי הכאב הוא דווקא מה שמניע את הפנייה ה: Perhaps the pain is precisely what drives the late address to his sons, his grandchildren and "the Children of Israel". The pain is not spoken, but it is present.
אילו קולות חסרים בסיפור המשפחה שלכם? מי: Which voices are missing from your family's story? Who can fill them in?
\"בני ישראל\" ולא \"עם ישראל\": "The Children of Israel" and Not "the People of Israel"
כותרת הצוואה, \"הנני פונה בקריאה נרגשת ל: The title of the testament, "I hereby address a heartfelt call to the Children of Israel", invites several readings. All of them rest on the text, and there is no need to choose only one.
טעינו בניווט הערכים (קריאתו של אמיר חודו: We went astray in navigating our values (Amir Chodorov's reading)
הרב פונה ל\"בני ישראל\" כי לדעתו טעינו ב: The rabbi addresses "the Children of Israel" because in his view we went astray in navigating our values, and we must go back and start again according to the principles of guiding values. The text supports this. The word "values" appears in it explicitly ("Please guard the values well"), and it was written during the Ten Days of Repentance. Repentance (teshuva) means return.
מי שחותם \"המוהל הנאמן והמסור לכולכם\" ה: The man who signs "the faithful mohel, devoted to you all" brought generations of the neighborhood's children into the covenant of Abraham. The "honored children" are, in a sense, his children.
במקרא \"בני ישראל\" הם השבטים שיצאו ממצר: In the Bible, "the Children of Israel" are the tribes who left Egypt and had not yet become a nation. In the desert they receive Torah and morals, and only afterwards enter the Land. The rabbi's ending, "I bore you on eagles' wings", is taken precisely from the moment of the giving of the Torah. Perhaps he seeks to found the people anew from the home and the family, and only afterwards as a state.
מה המילים \"בני ישראל\" אומרות לכם? אל מ: What do the words "the Children of Israel" say to you? Whom would you address that way today?
הערכים ושרידותה של שכונת התקווה: The Values and the Survival of the Hatikva Neighborhood
השכונה, כ־77 רחובות, שרדה 90 שנה בלי תכנ: The neighborhood, some 77 streets, survived for 90 years without planning, without a municipality in its early years and without resources. Amir Chodorov points to three core values that made this possible. Rabbi Avdar's life, as he himself described it, bears witness to each of them.
כך נסגר מעגל. הצוואה של שנות ה־80 היא קר: Thus a circle closes. The testament of the 1980s is a call to preserve the very values that allowed the neighborhood to survive, precisely when the rabbi feared they were eroding. "Please guard the values well."
איזה מהערכים האלה עבר אליכם מהבית? ואיזה: Which of these values passed to you from home? And which was almost lost?
מתי \"עשיתם לבד כי לא הייתה ברירה\", ומה: When did you "do it yourselves because there was no choice", and what was born of it?
הרב כתב שבעבר \"לא גנבו ולא רימו\". מה א: The rabbi wrote that in the past "they did not steal or cheat". What would you write to your grandchildren about your generation?
אם הייתם מוסיפים שורה אחת לצוואה של הרב,: If you were to add one line to the rabbi's testament – "Please…" – what would it be?
התמלילים שעליהם מבוסס העיון הם תמלילי עב: The transcriptions on which this reading is based are working transcriptions. Words not read with certainty are marked [?], and passages that could not be read are marked […]. Each document's page shows the transcription alongside the scan.

״אני יליד תימן, למדתי להיות שוחט ומוהל ו: "I was born in Yemen; I learned to be a ritual slaughterer, a mohel and a marriage officiant from the rabbis of Yemen"
האוטוביוגרפיה של הרב, בגוף ראשון, בארבעה: The rabbi's autobiography, in the first person, in four pages. He describes his ordination in Yemen and the long journey through the Far East: Singapore, Shanghai, Rangoon, Calcutta, Bombay and Peshawar. Then the attempt to reach the Land through Damascus in 1936, the years in Beirut, the arrival in Rehovot in 1939 and the neighborhood. At the end he turns to a rebuke about the state of society and housing prices.
העדות הישירה ביותר למסלול חייו, בלשונו,: The most direct testimony to the course of his life, in his own words, and a source for the neighborhood's three values.

אני יליד תימן, למדתי להיות שוחט ומוהל ומ: I was born in Yemen; I learned to be a ritual slaughterer, a mohel and a marriage officiant from the rabbis of Yemen and was ordained, and I married in the year 5686, 1926, and I left Yemen […] and my wife stayed in her parents' home. On reaching Aden I went […] to do work, returned to Aden and went to Djibouti [?], stayed 3 months and did not manage well, returned to Aden and to Yemen and kept Passover, and went back to Aden without a penny, for my father said he did not want me to stay [away] so as to serve in holiness with all that I had learned. But I decided to leave Yemen for good. I turned to my mother and my brother and asked them for money, and they gave me a little […], and I promised them I would not betray their trust nor my wife.
בחודש אייר 1928 עזבתי את תימן לצמיתות. ב: In the month of Iyar 1928 I left Yemen for good. On reaching Aden I arranged a passport and traveled to Singapore [?]. On arriving […] I saw that the pronunciation [?] and the manner of reading were different, so I decided to learn the accent thoroughly, and within a month I learned it very well with the pupils of the school, and on the Sabbath of Vayera I read the haftarah and read it in pure Sephardi pronunciation and diction. The congregation loved me, and I began to teach children […] I earned about seven rupees a month, but I was not satisfied with that.
עזבתי […] ונסעתי לשנגחאי באמצע החורף, וב: I left […] and traveled to Shanghai in the middle of winter, and on arriving there I could not endure the climate, and I returned to Singapore by way of Hong Kong – Saigon – Hawa [?], and from there to Rangoon. There I stayed about 3 months and did not succeed in finding work. I traveled to Calcutta and again did not succeed in finding work. Afterwards I traveled to Bombay; there I rented a large shop and began to teach Torah to children from the age of 5 up to bar mitzvah age, and I succeeded greatly […] I paid all my debts honorably.
אחרי שנה ששהיתי בבומבאי באו מפקיסטן, מעי: After a year in Bombay a delegation came from Pakistan, from the city of Peshawar, seeking a cantor and ritual slaughterer etc., and they came to me and I agreed with them on the salary etc., and I traveled with them by train for 3 days and 3 nights until we reached Peshawar. And the community was a worthy congregation faithful to the Torah of Israel, of the Bukharan community. Their trade was in the hides of kids and goats […] and they had homes in Jerusalem; they would come from Jerusalem in the month of Av and return to Jerusalem in the month of Nisan, and they would praise before me the Land of Israel and the Yemenite Jews in Jerusalem. And then a full desire entered my heart to turn to my parents' house in Yemen so that they would immigrate to the Land, and I would send them all their expenses.
וכן היה: מרי אבי מכר את כל רכושו ויצא עם: And so it was: my lord father sold all his property and set out with his sons and daughters and grandchildren, 15 souls in number, and on reaching Aden in 1933 they all entered the Land, to Rehovot. And my lord father […] stayed in Aden with my wife […]. I sent a letter […] that they should send a passport for my father and my wife and their children [?].
[…] אותם אליי לעיר פשאוור, וכן היה. בהגי: […] them to me in the city of Peshawar, and so it was. When they reached me I was very happy. My father […] for a period of a year and some months, and afterwards I sent him back to Aden, and in 1935 he immigrated to the Land and lived with his sons in Rehovot, and I stayed in Peshawar. A son was born to me named Eli.
ובשנת 1936 נסעתי לארץ דרך […] – בגדאד –: And in 1936 I traveled to the Land by way of […] – Baghdad – Damascus. On reaching Damascus I hired a taxi with an Arab driver and traveled toward the Land, during the riots that were then […] and he advised me to go back to Damascus […]. On reaching Damascus they gave me no work at all in the trade I had. I stayed 3 months without work; then they advised me to go to Beirut.
נסעתי לבירות, ובהגיעי שאלתי על […] הלכתי: I traveled to Beirut, and on arriving I asked about […]; I went to him and he came toward me. At once I went with him to the house of the community committee, Mr. Yosef Farhi. He immediately ordered the chief rabbi to examine me and check the slaughtering knife. He checked the knife and examined me in the laws of slaughter, and immediately gave me a permit […] cantor and teacher […]. And afterwards a second son was born to me […]. I stayed about 4 years, then I went up to the Land, to Rehovot, in 1939.
בהגיעי לרחובות עבדתי בפרדס ולא הלך לי. א: On reaching Rehovot I worked in an orange grove and it did not go well for me. Then I opened a heder to teach children and I succeeded. After 3 months they invited me to the Hatikva neighborhood to circumcise a child […]. I came and spent the Sabbath and prayed in the "Tiferet Israel" synagogue of the Sephardim. […] and they invited me to lead the Musaf prayer. I prayed, found favor in the eyes of the Sephardi congregation, and they asked me to be their cantor. I agreed for the sum of 40 grush a month, and I would also receive donations from the congregation […] and also teach children with the help of the synagogue and also slaughter poultry. After the agreement I traveled to Rehovot and brought my wife […] to the Hatikva neighborhood according to the terms, and I began to serve in holiness faithfully.
היו בשכונת התקווה 3 מורים תימנים שהיו מל: There were 3 Yemenite teachers in the Hatikva neighborhood who taught in a heder; there was no school at all in the neighborhood, and only a small number of the children walked to the Bialik school on Levinsky St. in Tel Aviv. […] I rose and wrote two letters – to the Mizrachi Organization and to the Histadrut – and said to both that the two institutions should open a school in the neighborhood. The "Mizrachi" […] and Dr. […], the chief supervisor of teachers in the Mizrachi schools, came to me, and we searched for a place for a week and found a two-story house in the Ezra neighborhood, and we opened it as a school under the auspices of the Mizrachi. The Histadrut did not find a place […]. Dr. […] was glad and charged me with taking a census in the neighborhood – how many children were without schooling. And within a week I counted more than 5,000 children who were without a school.
3 מורי החדר העבירו את התלמידים לשכונת עז: The 3 heder teachers moved their pupils to the Ezra neighborhood and were appointed teachers. I worked only one year and resigned […] I worked at […] in all the camps […] and it was very hard for me. I began to work in kashrut [?] […] and I have continued in this work to this day.
בשנת 1939, בהגיעי לשכונת התקווה, היה בה: In 1939, when I reached the Hatikva neighborhood, there were dozens of huts and houses of blocks and rickety foundations. All around Hatikva were orange groves. No street was paved except the main street, today Etzel St. […]. The "Shimshon" company arose, 5 people in number […], and began to buy the orange groves from the Arabs, and sold each plot according to the buyer's means – each pik [cubit] for 15 grush – and everyone built as he wished, without any supervision and without any plan.
השכונה הייתה תחת חסות עיריית יפו ותחת ממ: The neighborhood was under the authority of the Jaffa municipality and the Mandate government. The Tel Aviv municipality was under Mr. Rokach, and he […] did not want to annex the neighborhood to Tel Aviv. He said explicitly that he would have to invest millions to fix the neighborhood. And the neighborhood remained without any supervision, and everyone built as he wished. The neighborhood spread and grew, and the Ezra neighborhood arose beside it – it too was built without any supervision, by its residents who came from East and West. All the residents were poor, workers […]. The whole neighborhood was low-lying, full of swamps […].
בשנים 1940 עד 1956, במשך כל הגשמים, נכנס: In the years 1940 to 1956, through all the rains, [the water] came into the houses to a height of a meter and more, and they would bring boats and help […] and Magen David [Adom] to save them from drowning, and would take the people out to the schools […]. The public suffered more than enough from the heavy rains.
אחר התארגנו והקמנו ועד, שלושה אנשים, והם: Afterwards we organized and founded a committee of three people, namely: Yehuda Madar, Shalom Yefet, Shalom Avdar. The three of us signed a document and annexed the neighborhood to Tel Aviv through Mayor Levanon […]. And today the neighborhood has risen gloriously in terms of building, but […] for every person wants to settle in an apartment and set up a home, and he cannot because of runaway inflation and the high cost of housing, and the young have turned to ways the Torah forbade […].
לא תגנוב – לא תחמוד – לא תנאף […]. היהוד: You shall not steal – you shall not covet – you shall not commit adultery […]. The Jews […] kept in their exile the Torah of Israel and its laws, and today in the Land crime has multiplied. There are synagogues in the Hatikva neighborhood, close to […], for all the communities, and all are full of commandments like a pomegranate, keepers of the tradition of Israel. And if there are […] they are sorry and cry out and say: we came to the Land to be righteous and not wicked […]. Many have left […] for Bnei Brak – Bat Yam – Holon, and everyone who left the neighborhood regrets it. Why? Most of the teachers […] and little of the Torah of Israel […] and this is a gateway to ruin for the young and their parents.
היום […] קשה להשיג דירה שמחירה עלה למעלה: Today […] it is hard to obtain an apartment whose price has risen above a million – this is dizzying and saddening. In my opinion and in the opinion of the people, the government should build and hand over to Israel at reduced, reasonable prices for all, and not hand construction over to companies that make fortunes at the people's expense. And it is said: "The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine."
[…] על ידי אומות העולם […] ובאים אנשי חו: […] by the nations of the world […] and lawmen come and legislate laws […] not for the good of the people that aspires to build and to settle in its national and liberated land as one. This is a great absurdity that cannot be forgiven!

״תולדותיה של שכונת התקווה, מאת הר׳ שלום: "The history of the Hatikva neighborhood, by Rabbi Shalom Avdar, veteran mohel and cantor in the neighborhood"
כרוניקה בשני עמודים, ובה הרב מופיע בגוף: A two-page chronicle in which the rabbi appears in the third person. It tells of the orange groves and the "Shimshon" company, the neighborhood committee (Yehuda Madar, Shalom Yefet, Shalom Avdar), the opening of the school and the days of shelling in the war. It ends with the call "Be strong and of good courage" and a demand for fair housing.
היסטוריה של השכונה מנקודת מבטו של אחד ממ: A history of the neighborhood from the point of view of one of its leaders, and also a public testament.
תולדותיה של שכונת התקווה, מאת הר׳ שלום א: The history of the Hatikva neighborhood, by Rabbi Shalom Avdar – mohel, veteran cantor in the neighborhood […]
[…] בקרב עדת ישראל בארץ ובחו״ל, המשרת הצ: […] among the community of Israel in the Land and abroad, who serves the public faithfully. Rabbi Avdar immigrated to the Land of Israel […] and came to it in 1936, and went back to Lebanon, and stayed in Lebanon […] served the Lebanese community as cantor, in circumcision and in the slaughter of poultry […] and came to Rehovot to his parents […] worked in agriculture […] and he opened a class […] to teach them in Sephardi pronunciation.
בניסן 1939 נולד בן למשפחה […] בשכונת התק: In Nisan 1939 a son was born to a family […] in the Hatikva neighborhood, and they invited him to be the mohel for their son. On the Sabbath […] he prayed among the Eastern Sephardi community, and they invited him to lead the prayer, and he found favor in their eyes and they appointed him their cantor (mohel – teacher – ritual slaughterer). He moved his family to the Hatikva neighborhood […] all its surroundings were orange groves. […] the "Shimshon company" […] began to buy the orange groves from the Arabs […] each family […] according to their means, from the labor of their hands […] the neighborhood, without planning, suffered greatly […].
[…] בשנת 1949 קמה מדינת ישראל […] התארגן: […] in 1949 the State of Israel arose […] the neighborhood committee was organized, namely: Yehuda Madar, Shalom Yefet, Shalom Avdar […] a petition to the Tel Aviv municipality […].
הוועד […] בית ספר לא היה בה […] ילדי השכ: The committee […] there was no school in it […] the neighborhood's children walked to Bialik […]. The teachers: Avdar Shalom – tradition, Torah and prayer […]. Avdar Shalom […] to open a school […] took a census of children who were not studying – close to 3,500 […] and we found a house in the Ezra neighborhood, and the school was opened in it […]. The teachers were: Avdar Shalom, Tzubiri […] and also an Ashkenazi teacher, Halperin […].
[…] חברת שמשון […] האמינים באלוהים – והת: […] the Shimshon company […] believers in God – and synagogues began […] they did not know or hear of thefts […]. After the founding of the state […] the locals fought us […]
[…] הפגיזו וירו, והתושבים עומדים ברוח אי: […] they shelled and fired, and the residents stood firm in spirit in the great time when the enemy shelled the neighborhood […] until the army came […]. All the residents were one tribe in defense, and lived lives of freedom […]. Whatever they bought for their homes – all from the labor of their hands; they did not steal or cheat or rob, and lived lives of modesty and honor.
ורק בשנים האחרונות […] כמו כן הטלוויזיה: And only in recent years […] likewise television – the young began […] to watch films […] began to come […] violence – thefts – deceit – which the Torah forbade […]. Had […] the elected government placed great hopes in it […] none of the above would have arisen […]. And because of these deeds the neighborhood emptied of its veteran residents […] and today they look for a minyan and cannot find one, except from Sabbath to Sabbath.
שכונת התקווה הייתה המרכז הראשון לקליטת כ: The Hatikva neighborhood was the first center for absorbing every immigrant […]. The Hatikva neighborhood today is a center of happiness and wealth […]. We say: guard the faith, the tradition and the morals. Please fulfill "Love your neighbor as yourself", "each man shall help his fellow". Cease […] from cursing […] the neighborhood, which they built out of toil and suffering […].
[…] התאחדו והתלכדו ודרשו את […] מחיר הדי: […] unite and join together and demand […] the price of apartments […]. Be strong and of good courage, do not fear or be dismayed before them, for the land is given as a gift to all the House of Israel: "The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is Mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with Me." Think of the very best future, for your future and the future of your children forever, and be saved from evil.
חזקו ואמצו. מאת הרב שלום אבדר: Be strong and of good courage. From Rabbi Shalom Avdar

עמוד 3 [העמודים הקודמים אינם בסריקה]: Page 3 [the previous pages are not in the scan]
אני מבשר את בניי ואת נכדיי כי אני סגרתי: I announce to my sons and my grandchildren that I opened an account in your names at Bank Hapoalim 5 years ago, and your savings are growing, flourishing and shining […] and this is for your needs until your wedding day, that we may merit to rejoice in your joy.
תשורת זו אני מברך ודורש מכם שתבואו להתפל: With this gift I bless you and ask of you that you come to pray […] on the Sabbaths, and be good children […]. Persevere in a profession […] for your health, for your future. The sages said: learn much Torah and they will give you great reward. And beware of joining bad friends, and do not trust any friend, and ask your parents, who were tested with all the friends they had and who did not stand the test.
החברים של האדם הם: א׳ – באמונתם, הבריאות: A person's friends are: first – in their faith, health, one's wife and children.
אני והסבתא מריעים לכם ושמחים בשמחתכם, כש: Grandmother and I cheer you and rejoice in your joy, just as today we rejoice in the joy of the festival of trees, which renew their beautiful garments as they flourish – so may we merit your joy, your flourishing, your glory, your health and your success in life. May we and your dear parents merit to rejoice at your wedding canopy and in your descendants, and until the age of 120 may we all live in great splendor, tranquility and contentment […] amen and amen.

מהכלא ביפו לשכונה: From Jaffa Prison to the Neighborhood
לפי כתבה בעיתון \"חרות\" מ־1948, השכונה: According to an article in the "Herut" newspaper from 1948, the neighborhood was born in cell 6 of Jaffa prison. There in 1934 sat the men of "Brit HaBiryonim", among them Abba Achimeir and Yehoshua Lichter, and with them Abu Hadra, whose family held orange groves between Shapira and Kfar Shalem. Lichter came out of prison with a lease on the grove, and went into partnership with Standard Bank to build on it. This also explains the close link between Lichter, the bank and the guarding.
קיץ 1936: הבנק מחמש את השכונה: Summer 1936: The Bank Arms the Neighborhood
ב־17 ביולי 1936 נקראו 27 קונים לחתום על: On 17 July 1936, 27 buyers were called to sign mortgages in favor of Standard Bank. In the weeks that followed, at the height of the Arab Revolt, at least three rifles were bought from the same arms dealer (S. Rahmani): by Yehoshua Lichter on 18 August, by Dr. Dov Rosenberg, the Standard Bank manager who lived in the neighborhood, on 26 August, and by Aharon Yampolsky on 3 September. The recorded purpose is guarding and defense "in the Hatikva and Ezra neighborhoods".
הרובים עוברים מיד ליד: The Rifles Pass from Hand to Hand
הרובים הראשונים עברו בהמשך לשומרים אחרים: The first rifles later passed to other guards. Lichter's rifle (26645) passed to Arieh Pushtshik in 1937. Yampolsky's rifle (40595) passed to Yosef Feltzerman in 1938, "from Mr. Dr. Rosenberg, Standard Bank". Rosenberg's rifle (40672) passed to Mukhtar Shimon Rudi, from him to Zvi Dushnik, and possibly also to Reuven Mashkin and Pinhas Deutsch (in their files the number reads 40677). Mashkin also recorded that the owner of the land he guarded was Standard Bank. The picture is of a single guarding system: the bank equipped, the mukhtar approved and distributed, and the guards changed, to protect land still mortgaged to the bank.
שמות ומוצא: ניחוש בלבד: Names and Origins: A Guess Only
שם משפחה הוא רמז ולא הוכחה. תשעה מעשרת ב: A family name is a hint, not proof. Nine of the ten gun owners bear Ashkenazi names: Lichter, Yampolsky, Rosenberg, Deutsch, Mashkin, Pushtshik, Dushnik, Feltzerman and Mukhtar Rudi. The only one with a Mizrahi name, apparently Yemenite, is Ibrahim Sa'id Tzabari, who applied only in September 1938, and no license was found in his file. By contrast, among the 27 buyers in the mortgage notice most names are Mizrahi, many apparently Yemenite.
מה זה מרמז, ומה עוד חסר: What It Suggests, and What Is Still Missing
בשנים הראשונות התגבשו בשכונה שתי שכבות:: In the early years two layers took shape in the neighborhood: most land buyers were poor Mizrahi and Yemenite families, while organized guarding, the weapons and the connection to the bank and the authorities were in the hands of a small group of Ashkenazim. This is a hypothesis resting on ten surviving files, not on everyone who actually stood guard. Many guards may have served without a license, and they are invisible in the British records. The State Archives hold more files on the neighborhood (a complaint against the mukhtar, the village committee, drainage and flooding) that could complete the picture.

» \"בבית־סוהר ביפו הונח היסוד לשכונה עבר: » "In a prison in Jaffa the foundation was laid for a large Hebrew neighborhood"
״ראשיתה של שכונת התקוה — בתא מספר 6 של ה: "The beginning of the Hatikva neighborhood – in cell number 6 of the Jaffa 'Saraya'"
הכתבה מספרת שב־1934 ישבו בתא 6 בכלא יפו: The article relates that in 1934 the five convicts of the "Biryonim trial" sat in cell 6 of Jaffa prison: Abba Achimeir, Dr. Yehoshua Yeivin, Tavori, Orenstein and Yehoshua Lichter. In the same cell sat Abu Hadra, scion of a wealthy Jaffa family. Lichter came out of prison with a lease on several dozen dunams of Abu Hadra's orange groves, between the Shapira neighborhood and Kfar Shalem. He planned a housing estate, and being "penniless" he turned to Standard Bank and went into partnership with it. The grove was divided into plots and advertisements were published, but then the bank went bankrupt and the enterprise stopped. A young Yemenite named Malachi bought the land from the bank at a reduced price, and refugees of the 1936 riots came and built huts.
זה סיפור הלידה של השכונה, וממנו עולה שלי: This is the birth story of the neighborhood, and it shows that Lichter was the initiator and first developer. It explains the advertisements of 1935, the call to sign mortgages for Standard Bank in 1936, and the firearms licenses of Lichter and the bank's people that same summer. The document was written 14 years after the events, in the newspaper of the Herut movement, which saw Achimeir and his comrades as its founding fathers. So it is worth reading also as the movement's founding story, not only as testimony. The term "Biryonim trial" refers to the trial over the activity of "Brit HaBiryonim", not to the trial over the Arlosoroff murder.

״מסדר ועד השכונה פגישת חוכרי המגרשים על: "The neighborhood committee is arranging a meeting of the plot lessees over a glass of beer"
שתי מודעות מחודשי ההקמה: הזמנה לחוכרי המ: Two advertisements from the months of the founding: an invitation to the plot lessees "over a glass of beer" to mark the start of building and the laying of the water pipes, and the sale of plots at 40 grush per cubit, with a road and water at the sellers' expense and payments over two years.
התיעוד המוקדם ביותר לשכונה. המודעות פורס: The earliest documentation of the neighborhood. The advertisements were published in the Revisionist newspaper "HaYarden", with Jabotinsky's participation – an early hint of the neighborhood's link to the Revisionist movement and to Brit HaBiryonim.
ההזמנה \"על כוס בירה\" משקפת הוויה חברתי: The invitation "over a glass of beer" reflects a social custom common in the Land of Israel in the 1930s: an informal meeting around a drink, as a way to bind a community together and celebrate a beginning. The committee chose to open the building with a small celebration on the neighborhood's land, on a Saturday morning, before a single house stood there. The same custom returns in the neighborhood later: in 1943 the committee invites the participants in the general assembly to "a party over a cup of tea". The culture of meeting over a drink continued and developed in the following years, for example at "Kassit" on Dizengoff St., which opened there in 1944 and became a meeting place for artists and fighters. The 1935 invitation predates all of these and is one of the early pieces of evidence for the custom.

התנתן אספקת מים קבועה לשכונת התקוה: Will the Hatikva Neighborhood Be Given a Regular Water Supply?
כידוע, לא סופחה שכונת התקוה לאזור השיפוט: As is known, the Hatikva neighborhood has not been annexed to the jurisdiction of the Tel Aviv municipality. After its residents' opposition prevented its annexation to the jurisdiction of the Jaffa municipality, the neighborhood was included in Jaffa's town-planning area. In terms of responsibility for municipal services, it is a "no man's land".
מאז הקמת בתי המגורים הראשונים בשכונה לא: Since the first houses were built in the neighborhood, no satisfactory arrangement has been found for the water supply, which was in the hands of private owners who did with it as they pleased. More than once the neighborhood was left without water. A few weeks ago, too, the water supply stopped because of a broken motor. The residents, who can no longer bear these conditions, turned to the Tel Aviv municipality asking it to supply the neighborhood with water, as is done in other neighborhoods belonging to the Jaffa municipality.
עירית ת\"א הסכימה. אך להגשמת הדבר היה צו: The Tel Aviv municipality agreed. But to carry it out a special permit from the District Commissioner was needed. The residents turned to the Commissioner and received the answer that he had no objection to this arrangement. After making calculations, the municipality's water department informed the residents that 600 pounds would be needed to carry out the work, and 1,200 meters of eight-inch pipes to lay the main line. In a conversation with the manager of the Tel Aviv waterworks we were told that the government had agreed to allocate the money and the pipes.
אך בינתיים הודיעה \"חברת מפעל המים\" (הש: But in the meantime the "Water Works Company" (belonging to the "Shimshon" and "Standard" Ltd. companies) announced that it had applied to the District Commissioner for the water concession in the neighborhood and had already begun work. Since the "Hatikva" neighborhood is not within Tel Aviv's boundaries, the Tel Aviv municipality is not prepared to deal with its affairs and get into a quarrel over it. The people of the water company immediately began digging to lay the pipes (incidentally, most of the houses in the neighborhood already have connection pipes). These diggings aroused great anger in the neighborhood. Yesterday morning the trenches were found covered with earth.
מספר תושבי שכונת \"התקוה\" והשכונות הסמו: The number of residents of the "Hatikva" neighborhood and the neighborhoods adjoining it reaches 8,000 souls.

To His Excellency the Minister of the Interior of the State of Israel.
הנדון: ועד שכונת התקוה ועזרא. א.נ.,: Re: the committee of the Hatikva and Ezra neighborhood. Dear Sir,
יסלח נא לי כב׳ השר אם אגזול מזמנו בשורות: May the honorable Minister forgive me if I take up his time with these lines, but the matter is essential and concerns the health of more than twenty thousand souls of Israel, with God's help.
בשכונת התקוה קים ועד השכונה רק על הניר,: In the Hatikva neighborhood the neighborhood committee exists only on paper – or, more precisely, only for parties or meetings – but for public action, not even the smallest of the small.
והנה העובדות: א. הנקיון בשכונה אינו בידי: Here are the facts: a. Sanitation in the neighborhood is not in the hands of the neighborhood committee, but in the hands of a group of private individuals, and the committee has no oversight over the income and expenses of sanitation.
ב. המים בשכונה הם בידי חברה פרטית, ואין: b. The water in the neighborhood is in the hands of a private company, and the committee has no oversight over the income and expenses.
ג. בקופת ועד השכונה אין אף מיל אחד, בכלל: c. There is not a single mil in the neighborhood committee's coffers; in fact there is no treasury, no secretariat and nothing at all.
הפקרות צבורית של כל איש הישר בעיניו יעשה: Public lawlessness, every man doing what is right in his own eyes. One buys a hundred cubits of land and builds on all hundred, and another builds in the middle of the road. Is this to be called, sir, a committee? Could such a thing happen even in the State of Israel – to leave a populous neighborhood in such lawlessness? And what will become of the thousands of children playing in the filth and mud, for lack of even the smallest public garden?
ואם קורה חלילה ואחד התושבים מתריע נגד אנ: And if, God forbid, one of the residents protests against the sanitation men [who do not do what is required of them] – yet the taxes are collected all the same – and he, the resident, stops paying the sanitation tax in protest, then they punish him by dumping a great deal of garbage and refuse at his house.
זאת היא האמת על שכ׳ התקוה ועל כבוד השר ל: This is the truth about the Hatikva neighborhood, and it is up to the honorable Minister to put an end to the misery.
בכבוד רב, גד עבר, מזכיר ועדת הבטחון לשעב: Respectfully, Gad Ever, former secretary of the security committee.
עם ישראל יצא משעבוד לחרות. בדם בנינו ובנ: The people of Israel went out from bondage to freedom. By the blood of our sons and daughters the state arose and came to be. But a life of freedom and dignity does not yet sweeten our lives. The ills of the old regime still rule the life of our neighborhood and devour us with open mouth. The neighborhood's twenty thousand residents still live without all those services essential to every citizen of a free state.
אין שרותי נקיון ובריאות ראוים לשמם. וערמ: There are no sanitation or health services worthy of the name. Heaps of garbage fill our streets and carry disease into our homes and to our children.
אין בית ספר בשכונה. וילדינו נדונים להתגו: There is no school in the neighborhood. Our children are condemned to roam the streets without learning and to grow up ignorant in Israel.
אין טיפת חלב במקום. ואמהותינו נאלצות לשר: There is no mother-and-child clinic on the spot. Our mothers must make their way all the way to the soldiers' housing estate.
Because no one cares for the neighborhood.
כי ועד השכונה המכהן שנים רבות מפקיר ומזנ: Because the neighborhood committee, in office for many years, abandons and neglects the affairs of the working people's neighborhood.
כי ועד השכונה מתנשא על העם ואינו מוסר לע: Because the neighborhood committee holds itself above the people and gives the people no account of its deeds.
בזמן שלטון האויב הבריטי סבלנו מחלות רעב: Under the rule of the British enemy we suffered disease, hunger and ignorance. But in our own state we have the power to build our lives as we wish, to secure a humane life for the people of our neighborhood. It depends only on us – if we know how to organize, if we are of one hand!
אל נשב בחבוק ידים ונצפה עד שיגמרו המוסדו: Let us not sit with folded arms and wait until the institutions finish their deliberations about the neighborhood and its annexation to Tel Aviv.
נלחם לועד שכונה נבחר! ועד שיבחר על ידי ה: We will fight for an elected neighborhood committee! A committee elected by the residents will carry out their will and rest on street committees.
נלחם להקמת השרותים בשכונה וקודם כל את שר: We will fight for the establishment of services in the neighborhood, and first of all the sanitation services, which brook no delay.
נכנס אספות תושבים. נשלח משלחות שיציגו את: We will convene residents' assemblies. We will send delegations to present our demands to the neighborhood committee, to the Ministry of Health, to the workers' faction on the Tel Aviv city council. We will demonstrate our just demands before the municipality.
תושבים! הועדה היוזמת החלה בארגון התושבים: Residents! The initiating committee has begun organizing the residents to win the neighborhood's demands. Lend a hand to the action – success depends on you! In unity is our strength. Enlist – for a life of dignity for the citizens of our neighborhood.

To the Minister of the Interior of the State of Israel, HaKirya.
הנידון: תיק מס׳ 4/2/ע/אר 625. שר מאד נכב: Re: file no. 4/2/A/R 625. Most honored Minister,
הננו מתכבדים להפנות את תשומת לב כב׳ בקשר: We have the honor to draw your honor's attention to the affairs of the neighborhood.
ביום 26/7/48 ש.ז. כתבנו מכתב לכב׳ בדבר ס: On 26/7/48 of this year we wrote a letter to your honor regarding the annexation of our neighborhood to the area of the Tel Aviv municipality, and published the text of the letter in the daily press. At once a revolution took place in the neighborhood, and meetings upon meetings were held throughout the neighborhood, and the majority of the residents and all the house owners without exception opposed annexation and decided to demand from the government only a local council. A public committee was elected whose task is to approach the government with a demand to form a local council in the neighborhood, and also to demand firmly that the neighborhood committee follow their view and their decision and demand from the government only a local council.
לכן, לאור העובדות הנ\"ל, הננו להודיע לכב: Therefore, in light of the above facts, we hereby inform your honor that we cancel our previous request regarding annexation of 26/7/48, and join the view of the public in whose name we act, and ask your honor to approve a local council for our neighborhood as soon as possible, for the neighborhood is very large, with 20,000 residents, and its needs grow from day to day, and it is impossible to continue in the present state, when the residents want order and believe in a council that will impose order; for their part they are ready to pay all the taxes the council will impose on them, and they oppose the annexation of the neighborhood with all their might.
הננו מבקשים מכב׳ לשלוח לנו ולחלץ אותנו מ: We ask your honor to send to us and rescue us from this entanglement with the public, and to approve our request. We hereby enclose for your honor a copy of the memorandum sent by the public committee in the neighborhood to the neighborhood committee.
אנו מקוים שכב׳ יבין את מצבנו החמור וידון: We hope your honor will understand our grave situation and consider this letter seriously, for which we thank your honor in advance, and we wish your honor a good year, a year of success and victory, and quiet and tranquility in our state.
בכבוד רב, [חתימה וחותמת ועד שכונת התקוה: Respectfully, [signature and stamp of the Committee of the Hatikva and Ezra Neighborhoods]
The Committee for the Annexation of the Hatikva and Ezra Neighborhoods to Tel Aviv.
עם הקמת מדינת ישראל הרבה ידידים טובים בא: With the founding of the State of Israel, many good friends come to us to conduct election propaganda. They proclaim aloud: I will redeem the Hatikva neighborhood – and point to the disorder in the neighborhood. Everyone knows that nothing is done without financial means. The present committee has worked and works from its founding without any payment. The members are volunteers who give most of their time not in order to receive a reward but only for the good of the neighborhood.
לאחר שקולים רבים באנו לידי מסקנה אחת. וז: After much consideration we have reached one conclusion, and it is: immediate annexation of our neighborhood to the Tel Aviv municipality. Any other solution is like a poisoned gift that will bring only harm to the neighborhood. We will not lend an ear to propagandists and party agents who want to win the voters' votes with false promises.
שכונתנו היא חלק בלתי נפרד מן העיר. בה אנ: Our neighborhood is an inseparable part of the city. We are bound to it in everything: livelihood, work, services, schools, hospitals, etc., which to this day we receive from the Tel Aviv municipality.
אף אחד חוץ ממנה אם גם יבטיח לא יוכל לראו: No one but it, even if he promises, will be able to see it through and fulfill it. We do not believe, and will not believe, the braggarts who after the elections will leave without a farewell and leave behind only notices on the walls. We are like the Hebrew neighborhoods that were annexed to the Tel Aviv municipality; their former administration cannot be compared to ours. An end to private interests. The population should not be harmed because of discrimination and business. The Tel Aviv municipality bears the education of our children and their health, and cares for our poor and our injured. Who else could fulfill this role?
לסוכנים אנו אומרים: אל תדאגו לנו, מודים: To the agents we say: don't worry about us; we thank you – if you want our good, leave us to decide our own fate and the fate of our neighborhood.
Our demand for the annexation of the neighborhood and our request to the Tel Aviv municipality is a political one, and only the pressure of the foreign regime prevented us from realizing it. We want to be and to live like the rest of the city's residents, with duties and rights alike. We must not stand like a pauper at the door in return for "hush money"; we will not yield to force. The mothers, wives and children of our soldiers demand fair treatment and the elementary conditions of an orderly life, with regular sanitation, suitable children's institutions and medical institutions on the spot. Our demand of the Government of Israel and the Minister of the Interior is: do not treat us as stepchildren; we are equal to every citizen of the homeland in rights and in duties, and to this we are ready.
בברכת שנה טובה וגאולה שלמה, הועדה לספוח: With wishes for a good year and complete redemption, the Committee for the Annexation of the Hatikva and Ezra Neighborhoods to Tel Aviv.

מפלגת הלוחמים – כמפלגה השואפת ללחום גם ע: The Fighters' Party – as a party that seeks to fight now too the war of the broad masses of the people, the poor and the deprived – sees it as its natural duty to take part in, and even to organize, the hard campaign of the neighborhoods' residents – for their very existence.
אין הלוחמים לחרות המולדת יכולים לראות בש: Those who fought for the freedom of the homeland cannot look on with equanimity at the grave harm to the basic rights of the masses. The aim of our war for freedom was not to bring the people a regime of exploitation and abandonment of the masses. There is no national freedom without social freedom. Whoever does not see it so distorts the very concept of freedom and harms its essence. For freedom cannot be divided. A true fighter for freedom fights for the full freedom of the people in all its layers!
מתוך כך מעמידים הלוחמים את עצמם בשורות ה: Accordingly the Fighters place themselves in the front ranks of the battle on the neighborhoods' front, as on the other fronts. We therefore call on you:
תבעו את זכויותיכם! בל יפקירו מוסדות הממש: Demand your rights! Let not the institutions of the government and the city abandon the residents of the neighborhoods!
בתקופת הבחירות הבטיח מזכיר העיר מר גדיבי: During the election period the city secretary, Mr. Gadibi, promised a delegation of Hatikva residents who came to demonstrate over the terrible floods to begin sewerage works in the neighborhood immediately (six months ago). Then, in the election period, the honorable mayor promised the residents the whole world. Today they have forgotten their promise, because the election period is over.
אזרחי שכונת־התקוה! האם גם אתם שכחתם מה ש: Citizens of the Hatikva neighborhood! Have you too forgotten what was and what is about to be in the near future? Are you waiting for next winter's floods to remind you of the promises of those who abandon your children, your families and your property?
צו השעה הוא ארגון כל השכונה, ללא הבדל עד: The order of the hour is to organize the whole neighborhood, regardless of community, political view or party affiliation, in order to wage the fight for your rights!
יבחר ועד מהימן מטעם תושבי השכונה אשר יתב: Let a trustworthy committee be elected on behalf of the neighborhood's residents to demand your basic rights: a. Sewerage works in the neighborhood are to begin immediately. b. The demolition of houses is to stop, and negotiations are to begin between the elected committee and the municipality on building planning under municipal supervision. c. Electricity is to be supplied to the whole neighborhood.
תושבי שכונת־התקוה! זכרו! אלה זכויותיכם ה: Residents of the Hatikva neighborhood! Remember! These are your just rights, owed to you. Stand up for your rights with all firmness! The necessity of your existence demands an unceasing fight. Remember the great damage the malignant floods caused you! Remember the harm done to you by the demolition of your houses, which abandons many families who invested all their meager means in these buildings and leaves them without a roof over their heads. Remember, and fight for your rights!

פניה זו אליכם הינה פניה חריגה ומיוחדת, א: This appeal to you is an unusual and special one, arising from the mood prevailing today in other distressed neighborhoods in the country!
מטבע הדברים, היכן שמצוי אור, מצויים פרפר: Naturally, where there is light there are butterflies, and where there are financial means there are circles hoping to benefit from the means. And to that end, every means is legitimate in their eyes, even if it is violent and extreme.
ידוע לכם כמה קל לגייס אנשים להפגנות אלימ: You know how easy it is to recruit people for violent and ugly demonstrations in distressed neighborhoods; do you know how hard it is to recruit people for beautiful and useful cultural activity? Know this: it is very hard.
ועד שכ׳ התקוה קם על־מנת להעלות את קרנה ש: The Hatikva neighborhood committee was founded in order to raise the standing of the Hatikva neighborhood in the eyes of the citizens of the State of Israel, and to change the prevailing view that our neighborhood has only drugs, crime and violent demonstrations. For two years now the committee has been proving that there is far more human beauty in the neighborhood than was known!
היום רואים את השכונה באור הרבה יותר חיוב: Today the neighborhood is seen in a far more positive light, and the neighborhood's residents have the honor of saying to everyone: I am a resident of the Hatikva neighborhood.
אנו פונים אליכם מלב אל לב! אל תגררו להפג: We appeal to you from heart to heart! Do not be drawn into violent demonstrations!! No more shooting at helicopters! No more burning of policemen! No more neighborhood going up in flames!!!
יש לנו מערכת מחשבים ללימודי מתמטיקה בשכו: We have a computer system for teaching mathematics in the neighborhood, and we didn't burn tires to get it. We have a long school day in the neighborhood, and we didn't shoot at helicopters to get it. We have after-school clubs in the neighborhood, and we didn't beat policemen to get them. We have renovated houses in the neighborhood, and we didn't found a party to get them. We have "Beit Dani" in the neighborhood, and we didn't shout "charge!" to get it.
ישנן כמו־כן תוכניות נוספות לביצוע (חינוך: There are also further programs to be carried out (education – building – welfare), and we are pressing for them with full momentum.
השינוי בכל מערכת החינוך בשכונה הוא על הס: The change in the whole education system in the neighborhood is at the threshold, and we must not stop it from coming! Final soundings are under way toward launching an innovative building program in the neighborhood, and we must not stop it.
השכונה מגדלת דור חדש של נוער לומד ועובד,: The neighborhood is raising a new generation of young people who study and work; let us not shame them or stain their name. We will give them the best chances to compete as equals among equals in their future lives. We swear to do everything for their future! That is why we, the residents of the neighborhood, arose!
מחר יבואו אליכם פוליטיקאים, ויאמרו לכם:: Tomorrow politicians will come to you and say: go out into the streets and burn tires! No one in the neighborhood will gain anything from it! Those people who do not live in our neighborhood – they will gain from it! Please beware of this wild incitement, for the good name of our neighborhood matters to none of them! What matters to them is publicity!!!
דרכם היא לא דרכנו, ורצונם הוא לא רצוננו!: Their way is not our way, and their will is not our will! Please prove to them that in the Hatikva neighborhood a cultured generation is growing up, whose struggle is a cultured one, and to whom the name of the Hatikva neighborhood matters more than anything else!
עם כל האמונה שלנו בתושבינו, ועד שכ׳ התקו: With all our faith in our residents, the Hatikva Neighborhood Committee

אי שם בגולה מתקימת אספה ציונית. השמים יכ: Somewhere in the Diaspora a Zionist meeting is being held. The sky may be blue or grey, the sun blazing or cold, the wind may come from the north or from the south. None of this matters. Somewhere in the Diaspora, which has one character all over the world, the Zionists are celebrating some festival, or recalling a national mourning. They must gather in a hall of strangers, they must wear non-Jewish clothes, they speak a foreign language in the car, in the tram in which they ride to the meeting. Only the wish to resemble the gentiles is a Jewish wish, and within the alien surroundings a Jewish corner is created. Men and women take off the gentile mask, but they do not throw it away: let a cat scratch at the door, let a stone suddenly roll, and the mask is ready to be put on again. And now they try to put it on, but in their haste they cannot manage it, and the Jewish faces are revealed. Sometimes at a masked ball, after midnight, when the couples are tired and faces burn with heat, they take off the masks for a moment, and each tries to drink in the other's face with his eyes while the mask trembles in his hand. And when that moment passes they go on with the wild dances, and no trace remains of all they saw; and if there is one who remembers something, he hides it like a treasure in his heart. Such moments happen in Diaspora life too – on Herzl's memorial day or at the celebration of the second of November.
באותו הרגע הנהדר של חיי הגלות מופיע נואם: At that splendid moment of Diaspora life a speaker appears and tells about the Land of Israel. His manner of speech does not matter. His train of thought may be childish, but when he begins to speak a hidden spring of hope bursts forth and the imagination catches fire: there in the Land of Israel all the people are Jewish, the clothes they wear are Jewish, the spoken language is Jewish, the press is Jewish; there no masks are needed, there Jews can reveal themselves as they are. The heart contracts and yearns, and when the speaker finishes, "HaTikva" turns into a stormy song and hundreds of throats burst out, as if it were an oath! "Our hope is not yet lost."
אם אפשר הדבר, שבשעת מחזה שכזה יהיה נוכח: If it were possible that at such a scene a Jew were present who would not be moved by this song – say, a Jew who is not a Zionist, or who has only just become one and has not yet grown used to the essence of our national anthem – if such a Jew were present, the whole thing would look strange to him; to his "objective" ears the song bursting out with force and enthusiasm would sound like a sigh, and not like the expression of a national will. That is not how a people preparing to return and conquer the land of its fathers should sing; that is how a people sings that waits for miracles and does not even have the courage to voice its hope for a miracle, and is content to promise that the hope is not yet lost. But who will redeem the land? Who will sacrifice his life for the people? Yearning alone is worthless. A young man falls in love with a young woman, but if he sits in his room, alone within his four walls, content with the single consolation that his hope is not yet lost, another young man, braver than he, will come and take his beloved from him. Even young women today are not content with longing and hopes, but attain what they want. Only the Hebrew people goes on living a life of exile, and when a shining moment comes, the moment of awakening, it sings: "Our hope is not yet lost." Such a people cannot raise heroes, only supporters of Keren Hayesod and rattlers of collection boxes. And the "objective" Zionist says to himself: there in the Land of Israel, the land we have acquired anew, there they will not sing the sentimental and helpless "HaTikva".
במשך הזמן בא שנוי בחיי הציוני ה\"אוביקטי: In time a change comes in the life of the "objective" Zionist. He comes to the Land and forgets that we have not yet conquered it; he knows only one thing – that the newspaper under his arm and the language in his mouth are Hebrew, and his clothes are made in the Land. One night he visits a Zionist meeting – and it makes no difference whether the meeting is Revisionist, or of Mizrachi, or of the General Zionists B; the main thing is that it is Zionist and not Mapai. As he crosses the threshold of the hall, looks at the faces of those gathered and listens to the speaker, he has the impression that he has already once in his life been present at such a scene, has already seen these people and heard the speech... Exactly as there in the Diaspora, here in the Land too the meeting closes with the singing of "HaTikva" – the same song of yearning and passive hope, the same sad tone without courage. Is it with such an anthem that we will lead the youth to conquest? Such an anthem, it seems, can raise only a youth without strength, busy with polemics. In the Diaspora, before singing "HaTikva", they talk about money and about rattling collection boxes; here they already prove that neither giving nor rattling is needed. But the main thing is that they still go on talking about funds and boxes, and not about acquiring a land for a landless people. Not giving the money is the same act of "heroism" as giving it. Practical heroism is something else – and only then does the "objective" Zionist realize that the Land of Israel is a land that Balfour promised us, but not a land that we have acquired.
ה\"תקוה\" היא עדיין הפרוגרמה הציונית. ה\: "HaTikva" is still the Zionist program. "HaTikva" is our ideal. "HaTikva" is our means of struggle. Against all disappointments we have one remedy: "not yet lost"...
עד מתי עמי, תתגעגע ותקוה? האם אין גבול ל: How long, my people, will you yearn and hope? Is there no limit to it? Sometimes it seems that all the efforts are in vain, and that we will never get beyond hope. But beneath the ash-waves of disappointment the fire of the nation whispers. In the cooled blood of the individual the ancient generations begin to stir, and the voice of the generations, like the voice of a dead man rising from the grave, speaks to the fluttering heart: "The land was promised to you, but you must acquire it." And the song of hope rings as it is sung. The Song of Songs of the yeshiva boy bent over his book resembles the singing of "HaTikva" in the Diaspora. The Song of Songs of Solomon, who sang it in the vineyards as he searched for the Shulamite, was also a song of yearning – but full of youth and vigor. And so rang the "HaTikva" of the Zion demonstrators when they were sentenced to hard labor: the blast of "HaTikva" was then like the blast of a victorious army. Funds are not everything in the Land – the prisons will prove it. Sing, my children, "HaTikva" – but take heed that your song has the ring of metal, like the clash of swords in a war of liberation...

[...] ברשותו האדיבה אנו פונים אליו בשם א: [...] With your kind permission we turn to you in the name of the "Bnei Yehuda" sports association, which is active in the Hatikva neighborhood in Tel Aviv.
אם נכון זכור לו בקורו בשכונתנו ובלי ספק: If we remember correctly, you visited our neighborhood, and no doubt you also know the situation of the youth in this neighborhood.
תושבי שכונת התקוה המאוכלסת בצפיפות מרובה: The residents of the Hatikva neighborhood, which is very densely populated, [...] go out to earn their bread by toil and the labor of their hands, and often they are unable to meet their families' needs and to take care of their children.
רבים בני הנוער בשכונה שאינם מוצאים לעצמם: Many of the neighborhood's young people find no cultural or social occupation for themselves, and they gather in groups in the street [...] the cafés and the cinema and waste their time. Many long for something and do not know what to do with their time and energy.
במצב זה הבלם היחידי העוצר בעד התדרדרות ה: In this situation the only brake that stops the youth from deteriorating is sporting activity.
אנו, אגודת \"בני־יהודה\", ששמנו לנו למטר: We, the "Bnei Yehuda" association, have set ourselves the aim of caring for the physical and mental health of our neighborhood's youth.
We are far from party activity and disputes. In our work to develop sport in the neighborhood we are a peacemaking factor that calms spirits.
מרגישים אנו את אהדת בני השכונה הרוצים בה: We feel the sympathy of the neighborhood's people, who want activity expanded in all branches of sport: football, light athletics, gymnastics and other sporting games. So far we have not managed to find a serious source to support us and our work and to help us obtain a proper budget.
בלי ספק מרובים הם הצרכים שמשרד החינוך וה: No doubt the needs that the Ministry of Education and Culture [must meet] are many. Our modest request is that the honorable Minister will be good enough to listen [...] to the call coming from the outskirts of Greater Tel Aviv, a call that says:
שימו לבכם לנוער זה, בטרם יהיה עזוב ונעזב: Pay heed to this youth before it is abandoned and forsaken; help it to stand on the good and straight path!
נהיה אסירי תודה אם יורה כב׳ השר [להקצ]יב: We will be grateful if the honorable Minister will instruct that funds be allocated to our work from the education budget, or from sources he can find, so that we can continue our blessed work in our neighborhood, so that we can develop the physical fitness of the neighborhood's youth, who often suffer because of the hard conditions at home, and so that we can encourage their spirit and raise their cultural level, which is important to us socially and nationally.
נכיר תודה מרובה לכבוד השר אם יואיל להתפנ: We will be most grateful to the honorable Minister if he will be good enough to free himself for a short while, as soon as possible, to receive a delegation from our association for a talk on the above subject.
מצפים אנו לתשובת כבוד השר והננו חתומים ב: We await the honorable Minister's reply and sign with all respect and with the blessing of a healthy mind in a healthy body, · With comradely greetings, the "Bnei Yehuda" committee

צעיר יהודי ירה בשני יהודים בשכ׳ התקוה ·: Young Jew Shoots Two Jews in the Hatikva Quarter · The Wounded: the Mukhtar and His Brother · The Dispute: Over a Synagogue
תושבי \"שכונת התקווה\" הוחרדו בליל יום ד: The residents of the "Hatikva quarter" were alarmed on Wednesday night by the sound of shots in the house of the quarter's mukhtar, Yeshayahu Sharabi. It emerged that during a meeting of the neighborhood committee in the mukhtar's house, Yosef Shad, about 22, burst into the room with a pistol in his hand and fired several shots at the mukhtar, who was hit in the lower part of his body. The shooter fled at once and then ran to the neighboring quarter, where the wedding of a Yemenite couple was taking place at that time. At the wedding was Yosef ben Israel, 18, the brother of the quarter's mukhtar, and the assailant fired several shots at him too and wounded him seriously. A young man who tried to stop the shooter was stabbed by him and lightly wounded. A brawl broke out with the other young men at the wedding. Meanwhile two policemen from the Abu Kabir police arrived and arrested the assailant. The wounded were taken at once to "Hadassah" and operated on.
כפי שמוסרים תושבי השכונה, קדם להתנקשות ר: According to residents of the quarter, the attack was preceded by a quarrel between the two families over the ownership of the quarter's synagogue, which had been built by the assailant's late father. At 8 p.m. we were informed by "Hadassah" that the mukhtar's condition is satisfactory, while that of his brother is serious.
בן אחי המוכתר משכונת \"התקווה\" מת מפצעי: The Nephew of the Mukhtar of the "Hatikva" Quarter Dies of His Wounds
לאחר יסורים קשים במשך ששה ימים מת אתמול: After six days of severe suffering, the young Yosef ben Israel, nephew of the mukhtar of the "Hatikva" quarter, died of his wounds yesterday morning. He was shot together with his uncle, the mukhtar, last Wednesday night by the young Yosef Shad, over a dispute between the two families about the ownership of the synagogue in the quarter. The mukhtar's condition is already good.

מכתב לממשלת המנדט לקראת מסיבת עיתונאים ·: Letter to the Mandate Government ahead of a press conference · 30.7.1944 · Signed: M. Bentov
אדוני, הרשה לי להסב את תשומת לבך לעניין: Sir, May I take the liberty of drawing your attention to the following matter on which a statement from you at the forthcoming press conference will be greatly appreciated.
בקשר לתקריות האחרונות בשכונת התקווה ליד: In connection with the latest incidents at the Hatiqva quarter, near Tel Aviv, when a chronic shortage of water endangered the health and safety of about 6000 inhabitants, this paper has undertaken a private investigation into the background of the occurrences, which has revealed a very gloomy picture.
נראה שרוב אוכלוסיית שכונת התקווה נפל טרף: It appears that the bulk of the population of the Hatiqva quarter has fallen prey to an unscrupulous gang of land speculators, who have succeeded in evading or manipulating existing laws for their own benefit, with the result that confusion reigns as to the title-deeds, property rights etc., thus imposing on the settlers a state of virtual bondage to the speculators' companies.
נאמר שהיו אי־סדרים בהעברת הרכוש ובחלוקת: Irregularities are said to have occurred in the transfer of the property, in the allocation of the parcels, as well as in regard to town planning, water rights, etc. The water supply controlled by the said companies, besides being entirely inadequate, does not meet the minimum of sanitary requirements, one of the cisterns in use being open for bathing.
שיטה מתוחכמת של בעלות משותפת של קבוצות מ: An ingenious system of superimposed joint ownership of groups of settlers on a parcel held as "mushaa" parcels seems to have made a joint legal action a virtual impossibility.
כדי לבצר את מעמדם, נאמר שהספסרים ליבו סכ: To fortify their position the speculators are said to have fomented communal strife among the various sections of the community (Sephardi Jews, Yemenite Jews, etc.) and to have used the local mukhtar to further their selfish interests. This mukhtar is being accused of corruption, undue influence, blackmail and bribery.
לאור העובדה שרוב תושבי שכונת התקווה שייכ: In view of the fact that the majority of the inhabitants of the Hatiqva quarter belong to the poorest class, and that their whole position has been made precarious through methods over which they neither have, nor are likely to gain, control, it seems that Government intervention in the interest of public security and health is essential.
לכן אודה לך מאוד אם תוכל להבהיר: 1. אם ה: I therefore should greatly appreciate it if you could state: 1. Whether the Government would be prepared to appoint an independent committee of enquiry to investigate the situation and to recommend ways and means for settling the affairs of the Hatiqva quarter. 2. Whether the Government would be prepared to use without delay its emergency powers in order to requisition, temporarily or otherwise, the present water supply of the quarter and either transfer it to the Tel Aviv municipality or, failing that, appoint a controller to ensure proper water supply to the settlers as well as sanitary conditions. 3. Whether the Government is prepared to investigate the charges against the mukhtar and to remove him, should it prove that he does not command sufficient general support and respect of the whole quarter.
I am, Sir, faithfully yours, (Sgd.) M. Bentov.

לכבוד סגן מושל המחוז (המושבות) מר קופרמן: To the Assistant District Commissioner (Settlements), Mr. Kuperman, Southern District, Tel Aviv.
בקשר עם בקשתי להתמנות בתור מוכתר בשכונת: In connection with my request to be appointed mukhtar in the Hatikva quarter, and with the list of residents supporting it, I have the honor to add a short account of my life.
נולדתי בעזה בשנת תרנ\"ב (1892) לאבי המנו: I was born in Gaza in 5652 (1892) to my late father Nissim Elkayim, who was a member of the Ottoman high council in Gaza and one of the founders of the colony of "Ruhama" in the south of the country.
אחרי גמרי את ביה\"ס העממי בעזה נסעתי ליר: After finishing primary school in Gaza I went to Jerusalem, where I completed the course of study at the Shaki yeshiva and received ordination as a ritual slaughterer from Rabbi Nahman Batito, Rishon LeZion of the Sephardi community in Jerusalem. On the recommendation of the rabbinate I received in 1912 the post of slaughterer in the colony of "Har-Tuv".
בהיותי במצרים בשנת 1915 התגייסתי לגדוד ה: While in Egypt in 1915 I enlisted in the Hebrew battalion, the Zion Mule Corps. After two years of service I was transferred to the E.L.C., and in that corps I was the foreman responsible for carrying out various railway works with hundreds of workers (Railway Construction) from Kantara to Haifa, and telegraph works from Acre to Ras en-Naqura, until 1921. Afterwards I worked as a corporal foreman in road building from Tiberias to Rosh Pinna.
עם ייסוד שכונת התקוה הייתי בין המייסדים: When the Hatikva quarter was founded I was among the very first founders. During the disturbances in the country I stood guard here and worked hand in hand with the quarter's previous mukhtar in defending the place, and thanks to the great efforts we invested and our faithful devotion the residents stayed in their places, and so the quarter was saved from ruin and destruction, and we brought it to grow, flourish and spread to its present state; today it numbers some eight thousand people.
עם גידול השכונה ועם התרבות התושבים התרבו: With the growth of the quarter and the increase of its residents, the public matters requiring attention have multiplied, both within the quarter and in representing its interests before the authorities.
עד כה הייתי עסוק מאד בעבודתי הפרטית, אשר: Until now I have been very busy with my private work, which in no way allowed me to devote myself to public affairs; but the neglect of the quarter's affairs has reached such a state that hundreds of residents urge me every day to agree to take upon myself part of the quarter's heavy burden of work, which cannot be done by one man.
אני מרגיש בנפשי, בתור אדם המכיר את השכונ: I feel, as a man who knows the quarter and its residents closely, that I can fulfill the duties of a mukhtar to the satisfaction of the authorities and the residents, above all the residents who belong to the Sephardi community.
לבסוף אני מתכבד להסב את תשומת לב כב׳ למכ: Finally I have the honor to draw your attention to the letter of Mr. A. Elmaleh, member of the National Council of the Jews of Palestine, sent to you yesterday. · Respectfully, [signature]
