To the Assistant District Commissioner, Lydda District.
מ. מ. נ. אנו החתומים מטה, שמעון מלחי ואב: Dear Sir, we the undersigned, Shimon Malakhi and Avraham Nissim Elkayim, mukhtars of the Hatikva and "Ezra" quarters, wish to draw your attention to the following particulars:
1. גושי האדמות של השכונות הנ\"ל רשומים ב: 1. The land blocks of these quarters are registered at the Land Registry in Jaffa as Nos. 6135 and 6136 of the lands of Salama, and 6034 of the lands of Yazur, and the property tax for these lands is collected by the finance departments in Lydda and Ramle.
2. לפני זמן קצר הודיעו מחלקות הכספים הנ\: 2. A short while ago these finance departments announced that for every property-tax certificate on these lands, required for land transfers at the Land Registry, a poll tax of 5 Palestine pounds or more a year will be paid for the benefit of the Arab villages in the district, apart from the property tax regularly collected from these blocks.
3. מס הגולגולת הנ\"ל הנו מיועד לטובת הכפ: 3. This poll tax is intended for the benefit of the Arab villages and their inhabitants only, and is not intended for our quarters and their residents.
4. אנו מתפלאים על ההוראות שניתנו ע\"י קצ: 4. We are surprised at the instructions given by the district officers in these departments to collect the poll tax, at a time when no such instruction or law has been officially approved, nor appeared in the Official Gazette and been publicly published, so that we could give our opinion on the matter.
5. כל זמן שמס הנ\"ל לא אושר באופן רשמי א: 5. As long as this tax has not been officially approved, these finance departments are not entitled to collect it from our property owners; and if such a tax is finally approved, we demand that all its revenues from our lands be paid into the neighborhood committee's fund, in order to improve the vital and necessary services in these quarters, which suffer greatly from a lack of financial sources.
6. אנו מבקשים מאת כב׳ לעיין בבקשתנו זו ע: 6. We ask you to consider this request of ours, in order to suspend payment of this tax until it is clear to us what its nature is and to which institutions it will be paid.
בכבוד רב, החתום: מוכתרי שכונות \"התקוה\": Respectfully, signed: the mukhtars of the "Hatikva" and "Ezra" quarters. [The two mukhtars' seals: MUKHTAR, HATIQVA AND EZRA QUARTERS]
פלטיאל דיקשטין, עורך־דין · יצחק אורן, עו: P. Dikshtein, Advocate · Isaac I. Orren, Advocate · Tel Aviv, 29 August 1944 · Stamp: 12 SEP 1944
לכבוד מר י. קופרמן, קצין מחוז (מושבות),: To Mr. J. Kuperman, District Officer (Settlements), District Offices, Levontin St., Tel Aviv. · Re: Hatikva quarter. The residents' request concerning the administrative organization of the place.
1. ביום 21/8/44 נשלחה לכבודו הודעה בחתימ: 1. On 21/8/44 a notice signed by 3 members of the elected committee was sent to you about the assembly held on 20/8/44, with the resolutions adopted that day attached.
2. הננו להמציא בזה לכבודו תזכיר על מצב ה: 2. We hereby submit to you a memorandum on the state of affairs in the quarter, together with our proposals and demands for remedying the situation forthwith.
3. מצאנו לנכון להודיע שאספת התושבים האשכ: 3. We think it right to report that the assembly of the Ashkenazi residents of the quarter, held on 26/8/44, joined the resolutions adopted at the assembly of the Sephardi community on 20/8/44.
4. The first settlers came to the place in 1935. The surroundings were foreign and far from any organized Jewish settlement.
5. הקרקעות נרכשו מבעלים פרטיים שנצלו את: 5. The land was bought from private owners who exploited the buyers in various ways. No orderly division of the land was ever made, and the residents are paying for it and will go on paying.
6. מרבית התושבים – מבין עדות המזרח – נפל: 6. Most of the residents – of the Oriental communities – fell victim to greedy men who dictated the price, the terms of transfer, the keeping of the contracts and the amount of land transferred and the rights attached to it.
7. המעיין ברוב הקושאנים יוכח שהקונים רכש: 7. Anyone who examines most of the title deeds will see that the buyers acquired not only the ownership of the land but also an undivided share in a) the well and the water plant, b) the pipe network. Special sums were promised and paid for the pipes.
8. צורפו בזה העתקות מ־4 תעודות רישום, שב: 8. Attached are copies of 4 registration certificates in which the type of property is stated explicitly: "...with three rooms (that is, the water plant) from before 1331, and a well."
9. אספקת המים הפכה למקור לשחיתות ולשלטון: 9. The water supply became a source of corruption and of tyrannical rule over the people of the quarter; those who managed to concentrate it in their hands gained boundless power over the quarter's innocent people, as will be explained below.
10. מצוקת הדירות בעיר שעצמה בעיקר בשנות: 10. The housing shortage in the city, which grew mainly in the long years of the war, brought masses of new settlers to the quarter. Most were from the Oriental communities, who with their last pennies bought a plot of land and put up cramped buildings for their large families.
11. מספר התושבים נאמד היום ב־8000 נפש, מ: 11. The number of residents is estimated today at 8,000 souls, of whom about 65% are of the Sephardi community, about 30% Yemenites and about 5% Ashkenazim.
12. לרגל תמימותם של מרבית תושבי השכונה ו: 12. Because most residents are naive and wholly absorbed in their work, they have had no time for public affairs, and today this quarter holds a unique place as the most neglected of the Jewish settlements in the country. Settlements with far fewer people have been blessed with lawfully organized administrative bodies, elected and answerable to the whole public, while in the Hatikva quarter "the Middle Ages" rule everything.
13. בחדשים האחרונים גדלה האנדרלמוסיה ועל: 13. In recent months the chaos has grown beyond measure, especially because of the constant shortage of water, which the private companies not only failed to solve but are suspected of having done much to entangle for their own interests. This water distress is what made the progressive people of the quarter see the urgent need to find an immediate radical solution and change the situation from its foundations, forthwith.
14. \"השלטון\" הקיים בשכונה – המוכתר: 14. The existing "government" in the quarter – the mukhtar
לפני כשנתיים נתמנה אחד התושבים להיות למו: About two years ago one of the residents was appointed mukhtar. No one can understand what moved the District Officer to raise to this high rank a Yemenite porter lacking the most elementary education, who had never dealt in public affairs, let alone the affairs of a settlement larger than the town of Netanya. But once he was appointed and several other residents were attached to him, many hoped that if he did no great things, at least he would not stand as an adversary to the people of the quarter, and would act honestly.
15. אנו מציינים בכאב ובחרפה כי ימי כהונת: 15. We note with pain and shame that the term of the mukhtar, Mr. Yaish Israel Yeshayahu, has been a time of corruption and public venality whose like is hard to find even in the most backward countries. We take full responsibility for the truth of our words, and to support them we shall bring facts and testimonies taken down from reliable residents, so that the District Officer may see and judge.
המוכתר נעשה שותף לה\"ה רולא ויעקב שקבלו: The mukhtar became a partner of Messrs. Rola and Yaakov, who took over the water plant of the "Standard" company and became its sole owners. The water supply was highly arbitrary and the complaints never stopped; many residents did not receive this vital commodity at all. But for the mukhtar the water plant became a source of income, from time to time a gold mine. Every resident paid a fixed monthly fee per room for the water supply. Hundreds of pounds flowed into the pockets of the water-owning partnership, but no one ever saw a financial or other report of what was done with the money and how it was spent. When a resident wished to put up a building, the water company charged truly fabulous sums for connecting the network to the building plot. Here are a few examples out of many:
(מוצג ח׳) מאת יעקב כהן גבו ביום 8/5/44 ס: (Exhibit H) From Yaakov Cohen they collected on 8/5/44 the sum of 42 Palestine pounds, and another 10 pounds by promissory note. · (Exhibit I) From Israel Yosef Cohen – 12.500 pounds. · There were cases in which the water company was ashamed and afraid to publish the sums it received, and a new "wording" of receipts was drawn up. (Exhibits J, K) "The full price for the pipes has been paid."
סכומים אלה שולמו שלא כחוק מאחר שקוני המג: These sums were paid unlawfully, since the plot buyers had already paid for the water pipes, as shown above; and even if something had to be collected, the sums taken bear no proportion to the real costs, and such a state of affairs can only be the monopoly of a gang without conscience.
מכל תושב שעמד להקים חדר או בנין אחר גבה: From every resident about to put up a room or another building the mukhtar collected various sums, supposedly to obtain building "permits," or simply as protection money. He threatened those who refused with criminal proceedings for building without a permit and the like.
אנו מביאים כאן קטעי עדויות. מחשש התנקמות: We bring here extracts of testimony. For fear of revenge by the mukhtar and his band of supporters we do not reveal the full names of our informants, but their names are recorded with us and we are ready to provide them to you at any time.
התושב מ. (12): \"...בנינו חדר. המוכתר קב: Resident M. (12): "...we built a room. The mukhtar took 5 pounds. No report was made." · Resident B. (14): "Around February I built a new house. The mukhtar took 10 pounds. He gave me no receipt for this sum. He threatened that if they did not pay he would go to the police." · Resident K. (16): "When I began to build (at the end of 1943) the mukhtar came and demanded money for the building, or else he would bring the police... I gave him 15 pounds without a receipt, 3 pounds for water."
המוכתר הנהיג שיטה \"רקאטירית\" אמריקאית: The mukhtar introduced a typical American "racketeering" system of taking money from residents who traded in controlled goods. Negligence or delay in paying brought immediate "retaliation" – informing to the police, criminal proceedings, fines and imprisonment. The "good boys" who paid regularly were cleared of all punishment.
כדי לחזק את שלטונו ולקיימו בידו ארגן המו: To strengthen and keep his rule, the mukhtar organized a group of Yemenites from his family (his brother) and acquaintances, who imposed order directly and indirectly; whenever someone tried to organize a gathering, meeting or discussion not in the mukhtar's spirit, they carried out an organized attack and "beat up" the stubborn and the rebellious. On 16/7/44 "the mukhtar's gang" burst into the Sephardim's "Tiferet Israel" synagogue and beat people murderously. Three of the attackers – one of them the mukhtar's brother – were brought to criminal trial in Tel Aviv.
16. הסכומים שהמוכתר קבל עולים לאלפי לא\": 16. The sums the mukhtar received amount to thousands of pounds. No account was kept and no receipts were given, and no one ever received a report of what was done with them. The money went into the pockets of the mukhtar and his friends.
17. כשנתמנה למוכתר היה מחוסר כל רכוש ומש: 17. When he was appointed mukhtar he had no property at all and earned scant bread and scant water. Today the mukhtar has two houses worth over 2,000 pounds, and in addition an income from selling building materials. The mukhtar practices no trade or profession – yet he lives like a lord and money is always in his pocket, as every child in the quarter knows.
19. פעולות המוכתר נמצאות בנגוד גמור לחוק: 19. The mukhtar's actions are in complete contradiction to the Mukhtars Ordinance, 1942, and to the Village Administration Ordinance (Official Gazette 1944).
שאלת המים אף היא לא תמצא את פתרונה כל זמ: The water question too will not be solved as long as the mukhtar, who has an interest in the water supply from another source, represents the quarter; his personal interests are completely opposed to the quarter's. We hope the District Officer will see fit to answer us and heal the quarter's affairs: paving roads, regulating building, drainage and flood protection in winter, education, sanitation and lighting. Only an elected council, supported by the public and lawfully authorized to deal with all public problems, can put an end to the backwardness.
ביום 20/8/44 נתכנסה אספה רבה עם שהשתתפו: On 20/8/44 a large assembly was held, attended by some 500 men who together with their families make up about two thirds of the quarter's residents. Resolutions were adopted unanimously, and the residents of the Ashkenazi community later joined them at their assembly on 26/8/44.
22. אנו דורשים מכבודו על סמך האמור לעיל:: 22. On the basis of the above we demand that you: (a) dismiss the mukhtar from his post at once; (b) take all the necessary steps to hold elections for a local council according to law; (c) recognize the undersigned elected provisional committee as the lawful committee until the local council is elected; (d) summon the members of the provisional committee to an immediate meeting with you to discuss all the affairs of the quarter and the organization of local government there.
לתשובתו המהירה נחכה. בכבוד רב, חברי הועד: We await your speedy reply. Respectfully, the members of the elected committee: 1. Shimon Shemesh, chairman · 2. Gad Abbo, deputy · 3. Moshe Yarhi, secretary · 4. Yitzhak Izon, treasurer · 5. Albert Farhi · 6. Ben Zion Levi · 7. Eliyahu Azizo · 8. Shlomo Otriger · 9. Yaakov Futerman. (5–7: members of the finance committee)

מחאה גלויה · על חלול החג ביום ב׳ דראש־הש: An open protest · Against the desecration of the festival on the second day of Rosh Hashanah – in the Hatikva quarter
אנו, גבאי בתי־הכנסת שבשכונה, מוחים בזה ב: We, the gabbaim of the synagogues in the quarter, protest hereby with all force and vehemence against the mukhtar of the quarter, who incited a group of people to announce and call, precisely on the holy day, the day when the soul pours out its prayer before God on high, on the festival of Rosh Hashanah, a general assembly and elections for the new committee, to be held in a café on the second day of Rosh Hashanah at 3 in the afternoon.
המוכתר בעצמו עבר בבתי־הכנסת והזמין את הק: The mukhtar himself went round the synagogues and invited the public to take part in this assembly.
מעשיו אלה של המוכתר עוררו התמרמרות רבה ב: These acts of the mukhtar aroused great indignation among the public, made them forget and desecrated the rest of the festival, and stirred stormy arguments during the prayers; only with great difficulty did we manage to calm the agitated public from desecrating this holy festival and from causing bloodshed.
וכשנוכחו על התמרמרות הקהל, הודבקו בעצם ז: And when they saw the public's indignation, notices were again posted, at the very time of the shofar blowing, written by the organizers, announcing the cancellation of the assembly.
האם זה מתפקידו של אדם המשמש כמוכתר השכונ: Is it the role of a man serving as mukhtar of the quarter and chairman of its committee to stir up strife and cast hatred and turmoil among the residents on this holy day?
הננו מקוים, שהרבנות הראשית, הממשלה והמוס: We hope that the Chief Rabbinate, the government and the competent institutions will take real steps to bring at last an end to the desecration of God's name and to the quarrels in the quarter.

מעונות ילדים בפרברי העוני · הושלמו הבתים: Children's homes in the poor suburbs · The houses named for Hanna Rovina and Malka Matalon are completed
\"בית חנה רובינא\" בשכונת התקוה ו\"בית מ: "Beit Hanna Rovina" in the Hatikva quarter and "Beit Malka Matalon" in Givat Moshe (the Shapira quarter) are the two new buildings now added to the Working Mothers' Organization, to serve as a shelter and place of education for children of the poor and of immigrants in the suburbs of Tel Aviv.
בסיור בשני הבנינים, שנערך ביום א׳ עם גמר: On a tour of the two buildings held on Sunday, on the completion of their construction, Dvorah Nosovitzky gave journalists details of the Working Mothers' Organization's activities for the child, and explained the roles of the new houses. The house named for Hanna Rovina was built next to the market of the Hatikva quarter, in its very heart. It has two floors and is intended for 300 children. It has 3 kindergartens and 3 day-care classes for school-age children. The first sum for the building was given by H. Rovina from the money of the Tel Aviv Municipality's art prize. The house named for Malka Matalon is intended for 100 children; the plot is a gift of the Matalon family in memory of the family's mother.
למעלה מ־30 אלף לא\"י עלתה בנייתם של שני: The construction of the two buildings cost more than 30 thousand Palestine pounds. Two thirds of the sum came from the women's league in America for working Palestine, the "Pioneer Women." The last third will be collected in the country, through the "a brick for the building" campaign.
פתיחתם הרשמית של שני הבנינים תהיה ביום 3: The official opening of the two buildings will take place on 3 July at the "Habima" house, with the participation of Hanna Rovina, Golda Meyerson, Beba Idelson and a line of artists.

מי ידבר בשם השכונה מול השלטון הבריטי? שת: Who would speak for the neighborhood before the British authorities? Twelve years of appointments, shootings, petitions and assemblies, until the government appointed two mukhtars: one for the Yemenites and one for the Sephardim.
בשנים הראשונות היה לשכונה מוכתר אחד, שמע: In its first years the neighborhood had a single mukhtar, Shimon Rudi. He approved the guards' gun licenses, and Avraham Elkayim later recalled working "hand in hand with the previous mukhtar" to defend the neighborhood during the disturbances. By 1941 there was no mukhtar. The committee wrote to the District Officer that "when there is no mukhtar, every man does what is right in his own eyes," and asked him to appoint one who would end the disputes among the committee members. In December 1941 the District Officer decided to appoint a mukhtar, because every attempt to make the committee work had "come to nothing." Letters of recommendation for candidates reached his office at once.
המוכתר שמונה היה ישעיהו ישראל שרעבי, תימ: The mukhtar appointed was Yeshayahu Israel Sharabi, a Yemenite. A newspaper report tells how a young man named Yosef Shad burst into a neighborhood committee meeting at the mukhtar's house and shot him, then shot the mukhtar's nephew, who died of his wounds six days later. According to residents, the background was a quarrel between two families over the ownership of the synagogue. The date is uncertain: the clipping is marked 1942, and the State Archives hold a coroner's inquest file on "Yosef Sharafy" from late 1941.
1944: מים, בריונים ואספת ה־500: 1944: water, thugs and the assembly of 500
בקיץ 1944 הגיע משבר המים לשיא. התושבים ה: In the summer of 1944 the water crisis peaked. Residents complained that the mukhtar summoned Yemenites "every evening" to beat and wound his opponents. A journalist, M. Bentov, probably Mordechai Bentov of "Al HaMishmar," wrote to the government that land speculators controlled the water, fanned communal strife and used the mukhtar, and asked for a commission of inquiry. On 20 August some 500 Sephardi heads of household gathered in the "Hesed ve-Emet" synagogue, declared no confidence in the mukhtar and demanded elections for a local council. Three members of the appointed committee resigned.
1945: שני מוכתרים, אחד לכל עדה: 1945: two mukhtars, one for each community
ביוני 1945 התפטר ישעיהו ישראל, ומינויו ה: In June 1945 Yeshayahu Israel resigned, and his appointment ended on 1 July. A war of petitions began at once. Yehezkel Shoshani wrote in the name of 250 families against four candidates. Avraham Elkayim, a Gaza-born cart driver and one of the neighborhood's veterans, sent his life story and a list of Sephardi supporters. The rabbis of the Yemenite community unanimously chose Shimon Malakhi. The police checked both men: according to the report, Sephardim and Yemenites were 45% each and Ashkenazim about 10%, and both candidates were "recommended." On 9 October 1945 the District Commissioner appointed both. The government settled the struggle by dividing it between the communities.
הפתרון שלא החזיק: The solution that did not hold
שנה אחר כך כבר כתבו נכבדי העדה התימנית נ: A year later the Yemenite notables were already writing against "their own" mukhtar, Malakhi. They claimed he was one of the managers of the "Shimshon" company, which sold the plots and controlled the water, and asked to bring back Yeshayahu Israel. A 1946 newspaper article also described a committee that had never been elected, which held the plots, the water and the sanitation, and from which both mukhtars had come. Yet in 1947 the two mukhtars signed a joint petition against a poll tax imposed on landowners for the benefit of the Arab villages. With the annexation to Tel Aviv at the end of 1948 the mukhtar's role came to an end. The State Archives hold more files not yet examined, among them a file titled "Complaint against the mukhtar of Hatiqva quarter," 1944–1946.

המוכתר שמונה היה ישעיהו ישראל שרעבי, תימ: The mukhtar appointed was Yeshayahu Israel Sharabi, a Yemenite. A newspaper report tells how a young man named Yosef Shad burst into a neighborhood committee meeting at the mukhtar's house and shot him, then shot the mukhtar's nephew, who died of his wounds six days later. According to residents, the background was a quarrel between two families over the ownership of the synagogue. The clipping is marked 1942, and according to a memorandum by his opponents from August 1944 the mukhtar had been appointed "about two years ago." The coroner's inquest file on "Yosef Sharafy" from late 1941, which at first seemed related, turned out to be a different case: an 8-year-old boy run over by a bus.
בקיץ 1944 הגיע משבר המים לשיא. התושבים ה: In the summer of 1944 the water crisis peaked. Residents complained that the mukhtar summoned Yemenites "every evening" to beat and wound his opponents. A journalist, M. Bentov, probably Mordechai Bentov of "Al HaMishmar," wrote to the government that land speculators controlled the water, fanned communal strife and used the mukhtar, and asked for a commission of inquiry. On 20 August some 500 Sephardi heads of household gathered in the "Hesed ve-Emet" synagogue, declared no confidence in the mukhtar and demanded elections for a local council. Three members of the appointed committee resigned, and nine men formed an "elected committee." In a memorandum sent to the government through lawyers, they accused the mukhtar of collecting money for building "permits" and for water, of a "racketeering system" and of a reign of terror enforced by his relatives. According to the memorandum, the neighborhood had 8,000 souls: 65% Sephardim, 30% Yemenites and 5% Ashkenazim. But the mukhtar had supporters too: dozens of heads of household signed a petition expressing "full confidence" in him and the committee, and demanding that the "new committee" not be recognized. On Rosh Hashanah 1944 the conflict reached the synagogues: the gabbaim of seven synagogues protested that the mukhtar had invited the public to an election assembly on the festival itself.
במאי 1945 הודיעה הממשלה לישעיהו ישראל שה: In May 1945 the government informed Yeshayahu Israel that it had decided to relieve him "in view of the numerous complaints," and asked him to show cause. In June he resigned, and his appointment ended on 1 July. A war of petitions began at once. Yehezkel Shoshani wrote in the name of 250 families against four candidates. Avraham Elkayim, a Gaza-born cart driver and one of the neighborhood's veterans, sent his life story and a list of Sephardi supporters. The rabbis of the Yemenite community unanimously chose Shimon Malakhi. The police checked both men: according to the report, Sephardim and Yemenites were 45% each and Ashkenazim about 10%, and both candidates were "recommended." These figures are worth comparing with the elected committee's memorandum: each side counted the neighborhood differently. On 9 October 1945 the District Commissioner appointed both. The government settled the struggle by dividing it between the communities.
ב־1946 החליטה הממשלה להקים בשכונה מועצה: In 1946 the government decided to set up a local council in the neighborhood. Elkayim wrote that he was "glad" of the decision, which would free the neighborhood from more than ten years of "lawlessness," and on 4 April 1946 the two mukhtars, Yeshayahu Israel and the men of the elected committee sat around one table at the District Officer's office. But the calm did not last. A 1946 newspaper article described a committee that had never been elected, which held the plots, the water and the sanitation, and from which both mukhtars had come. In November 1946 the Yemenite notables wrote against "their own" mukhtar, Malakhi: they claimed he was one of the managers of the "Shimshon" company, which sold the plots and controlled the water, and asked to bring back Yeshayahu Israel. In 1947 the two mukhtars signed a joint petition against a poll tax imposed on landowners for the benefit of the Arab villages. With the annexation to Tel Aviv at the end of 1948 the mukhtar's role came to an end. The State Archives hold more material not yet studied in depth, including the residents' statements collected by the police in 1945 and the file on the local council elections.
האלימות סביב המוכתרות התחילה כבר בשנים ה: The violence around the post of mukhtar began early. The clipping is marked 1942, which fits the 1944 memorandum saying the mukhtar had been appointed "about two years ago."
תזכיר בן חמישה עמודים שהגישו תשעת חברי ה: A five-page memorandum submitted by the nine members of the elected committee after the assembly of 500. It describes the neighborhood's beginnings, the land sold without orderly division, and the water plant that became a "source of corruption." According to the memorandum, the neighborhood had 8,000 souls: 65% Sephardim, 30% Yemenites and 5% Ashkenazim. Against the mukhtar it brings testimonies of money collected without receipts, a "racketeering system" and a reign of terror. It demands that the mukhtar be dismissed, the provisional committee recognized and elections held for a local council.
עשרות ראשי משפחות מצהירים על \"אימון מלא: Dozens of heads of household declare "full confidence" in the committee and the mukhtar approved by the government, and ask the authorities not to recognize the "new committee," which they say brings "disorder, quarrels and hatred between brothers" into the neighborhood. הגבאים מוחים על כך שהמוכתר עבר בבתי הכנס: The gabbaim protest that the mukhtar went round the synagogues inviting the public to an assembly and elections for a new committee, in a café, on the second day of Rosh Hashanah. They say the public was indignant, there were arguments during prayers, and bloodshed was barely avoided. In the margin a British official noted that negotiations were under way to strengthen the committee.

According to the article, every resident must pay the mukhtar a monthly fee for sanitation and for water per room, yet there is no water and no sanitation. The lawyer Orren, who handled the neighborhood's affairs, demands an "administrative organization," that is, a local council, and not putting off the matter until after the war. The clipping is kept in the government file, together with other articles from the same weeks on "the plight of Hatikva."

ב־1947 נפתח כאן \"בית חנה רובינא\", מעון: In 1947 "Beit Hanna Rovina" opened here, a day-care center and kindergartens of the Working Mothers' Organization, and Rovina herself cut the ribbon. Today the building houses the acting studio founded by Yoram Loewenstein in 1988. The students volunteer in the community.
